text_en: The works of God are done in judgment from the beginning, and from the making of them he distinguished their parts, and their beginnings in their generations .
text_la: In judicio Dei opera ejus ab initio, et ab institutione ipsorum distinxit partes illorum, et initia eorum in gentibus suis.
text_el: ἐν κρίσει κυρίου τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἀπ' ἀρχῆς καὶ ἀπὸ ποιήσεως αὐτῶν διέστειλεν μερίδας αὐτῶν

text_en: He beautified their works for ever, they have neither hungered, nor laboured, and they have not ceased from their works.
text_la: Ornavit in æternum opera illorum : nec esurierunt, nec laboraverunt, et non destiterunt ab operibus suis.
text_el: ἐκόσμησεν εἰς αἰῶνα τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς αὐτῶν εἰς γενεὰς αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐπείνασαν οὔτε ἐκοπίασαν καὶ οὐκ ἐξέλιπον ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν

text_en: Nor shall any of them straiten his neighbour at any time.
text_la: Unusquisque proximum sibi non angustiabit in æternum :
text_el: ἕκαστος τὸν πλησίον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐξέθλιψεν

text_en: Be not incredulous to his word.
text_la: non sis incredibilis verbo illius.
text_el: καὶ ἕως αἰῶνος οὐκ ἀπειθήσουσιν τοῦ ῥήματος αὐτοῦ

text_en: After this God looked upon the earth, and filled it with his goods.
text_la: Post hæc Deus in terram respexit, et implevit illam bonis suis :
text_el: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα κύριος εἰς τὴν γῆν ἐπέβλεψεν καὶ ἐνέπλησεν αὐτὴν τῶν ἀγαθῶν αὐτοῦ

text_en: The soul of every living thing has shown forth before the face thereof, and into it they return again.
text_la: anima omnis vitalis denuntiavit ante faciem ipsius, et in ipsam iterum reversio illorum.
text_el: ψυχῇ παντὸς ζῴου ἐκάλυψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτῆς καὶ εἰς αὐτὴν ἡ ἀποστροφὴ αὐτῶν

text_en: God created man of the earth, and made him after his own image.
text_la: Deus creavit de terra hominem, et secundum imaginem suam fecit illum :
text_el: κύριος ἔκτισεν ἐκ γῆς ἄνθρωπον

text_en: And he turned him into it again, and clothed him with strength according to himself.
text_la: et iterum convertit illum in ipsam, et secundum se vestivit illum virtute.
text_el: καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστρεψεν αὐτὸν εἰς αὐτήν

text_en: He gave him the number of his days and time, and gave him power over all things that are upon the earth.
text_la: Numerum dierum et tempus dedit illi, et dedit illi potestatem eorum quæ sunt super terram.
text_el: ἡμέρας ἀριθμοῦ καὶ καιρὸν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν ἐπ' αὐτῆς καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἐνέδυσεν αὐτοὺς ἰσχὺν καὶ κατ' εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς

text_en: He put the fear of him upon all flesh, and he had dominion over beasts and fowls.
text_la: Posuit timorem illius super omnem carnem, et dominatus est bestiarum et volatilium.
text_el: ἔθηκεν τὸν φόβον αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πάσης σαρκὸς καὶ κατακυριεύειν θηρίων καὶ πετεινῶν

text_en: He created of him a helpmate like to himself, he gave them counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, and ears, and a heart to devise: and he filled them with the knowledge of understanding.
text_la: Creavit ex ipso adjutorium simile sibi : consilium, et linguam, et oculos, et aures, et cor dedit illis excogitandi, et disciplina intellectus replevit illos.
text_el: διαβούλιον καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ ὀφθαλμούς ὦτα καὶ καρδίαν ἔδωκεν διανοεῖσθαι αὐτοῖς

text_en: He created in them the science of the spirit, he fired their heart with wisdom, and showed them both good and evil .
text_la: Creavit illis scientiam spiritus, sensu implevit cor illorum, et mala et bona ostendit illis.
text_el: ἐπιστήμην συνέσεως ἐνέπλησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ ἀγαθὰ καὶ κακὰ ὑπέδειξεν αὐτοῖς

text_en: He set his eye upon their hearts to show them the greatness of his works:
text_la: Posuit oculum suum super corda illorum, ostendere illis magnalia operum suorum :
text_el: ἔθηκεν τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν δεῖξαι αὐτοῖς τὸ μεγαλεῖον τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ

text_en: That they might praise the name which he has sanctified : and glory in his wondrous act that they might declare the glorious things of his works.
text_la: ut nomen sanctificationis collaudent, et gloriari in mirabilibus illius; ut magnalia enarrent operum ejus.
text_el: καὶ ὄνομα ἁγιασμοῦ αἰνέσουσιν ἵνα διηγῶνται τὰ μεγαλεῖα τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ

text_en: Moreover he gave them instructions, and the law of life for an inheritance.
text_la: Addidit illis disciplinam, et legem vitæ hæreditavit illos.
text_el: προσέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ἐπιστήμην καὶ νόμον ζωῆς ἐκληροδότησεν αὐτοῖς

text_en: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and he showed them his justice and judgments.
text_la: Testamentum æternum constituit cum illis, et justitiam et judicia sua ostendit illis.
text_el: διαθήκην αἰῶνος ἔστησεν μετ' αὐτῶν καὶ τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ ὑπέδειξεν αὐτοῖς

text_en: And their eye saw the majesty of his glory , and their ears heard his glorious voice, and he said to them: Beware of all iniquity .
text_la: Et magnalia honoris ejus vidit oculus illorum, et honorem vocis audierunt aures illorum. Et dixit illis : Attendite ab omni iniquo.
text_el: μεγαλεῖον δόξης εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν καὶ δόξαν φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἤκουσεν τὸ οὖς αὐτῶν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς προσέχετε ἀπὸ παντὸς ἀδίκου

text_en: And he gave to every one of them commandment concerning his neighbour.
text_la: Et mandavit illis unicuique de proximo suo.
text_el: καὶ ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ἑκάστῳ περὶ τοῦ πλησίον

text_en: Their ways are always before him, they are not hidden from his eyes.
text_la: Viæ illorum coram ipso sunt semper : non sunt absconsæ ab oculis ipsius.
text_el: αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτῶν ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ διὰ παντός οὐ κρυβήσονται ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ

text_en: Over every nation he set a ruler.
text_la: In unamquamque gentem præposuit rectorem :
text_el: ἑκάστῳ ἔθνει κατέστησεν ἡγούμενον

text_en: And Israel was made the manifest portion of God .
text_la: et pars Dei Israël facta est manifesta.
text_el: καὶ μερὶς κυρίου Ισραηλ ἐστίν

text_en: And all their works are as the sun in the sight of God : and his eyes are continually upon their ways.
text_la: Et omnia opera illorum velut sol in conspectu Dei : et oculi ejus sine intermissione inspicientes in viis eorum.
text_el: ἅπαντα τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐνδελεχεῖς ἐπὶ τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν

text_en: Their covenants were not hid by their iniquity , and all their iniquities are in the sight of God .
text_la: Non sunt absconsa testamenta per iniquitatem illorum, et omnes iniquitates eorum in conspectu Dei.
text_el: οὐκ ἐκρύβησαν αἱ ἀδικίαι αὐτῶν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῶν ἔναντι κυρίου

text_en: The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and shall preserve the grace of a man as the apple of the eye:
text_la: Eleemosyna viri quasi signaculum cum ipso, et gratiam hominis quasi pupillam conservabit.
text_el: ἐλεημοσύνη ἀνδρὸς ὡς σφραγὶς μετ' αὐτοῦ καὶ χάριν ἀνθρώπου ὡς κόρην συντηρήσει

text_en: And afterward he shall rise up, and shall render them their reward, to every one upon their own head, and shall turn them down into the bowels of the earth.
text_la: Et postea resurget, et retribuet illis retributionem, unicuique in caput ipsorum, et convertet in interiores partes terræ.
text_el: μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξαναστήσεται καὶ ἀνταποδώσει αὐτοῖς καὶ τὸ ἀνταπόδομα αὐτῶν εἰς κεφαλὴν αὐτῶν ἀποδώσει

text_en: But to the penitent he has given the way of justice , and he has strengthened them that were fainting in patience, and has appointed to them the lot of truth .
text_la: Pœnitentibus autem dedit viam justitiæ, et confirmavit deficientes sustinere, et destinavit illis sortem veritatis.
text_el: πλὴν μετανοοῦσιν ἔδωκεν ἐπάνοδον καὶ παρεκάλεσεν ἐκλείποντας ὑπομονήν

text_en: Turn to the Lord , and forsake your sins :
text_la: Convertere ad Dominum, et relinque peccata tua :
text_el: ἐπίστρεφε ἐπὶ κύριον καὶ ἀπόλειπε ἁμαρτίας

text_en: Make your prayer before the face of the Lord , and offend less.
text_la: precare ante faciem Domini, et minue offendicula.
text_el: δεήθητι κατὰ πρόσωπον καὶ σμίκρυνον πρόσκομμα

text_en: Return to the Lord , and turn away from your injustice , and greatly hate abomination.
text_la: Revertere ad Dominum, et avertere ab injustitia tua, et nimis odito execrationem :
text_el: ἐπάναγε ἐπὶ ὕψιστον καὶ ἀπόστρεφε ἀπὸ ἀδικίας καὶ σφόδρα μίσησον βδέλυγμα ὑψίστῳ τίς αἰνέσει ἐν ᾅδου

text_en: And know the justices and judgments of God , and stand firm in the lot set before you, and in prayer to the most high God .
text_la: et cognosce justitias et judicia Dei, et sta in sorte propositionis, et orationis altissimi Dei.

text_en: Go to the side of the holy age, with them that live and give praise to God .
text_la: In partes vade sæculi sancti, cum vivis et dantibus confessionem Deo.
text_el: ἀντὶ ζώντων καὶ διδόντων ἀνθομολόγησιν

text_en: Tarry not in the error of the ungodly, give glory before death. Praise perishes from the dead as nothing.
text_la: Non demoreris in errore impiorum : ante mortem confitere : a mortuo, quasi nihil, perit confessio.
text_el: ἀπὸ νεκροῦ ὡς μηδὲ ὄντος ἀπόλλυται ἐξομολόγησις

text_en: Give thanks whilst you are living, whilst you are alive and in health you shall give thanks, and shall praise God , and shall glory in his mercies.
text_la: Confiteberis vivens, vivus et sanus confiteberis : et laudabis Deum, et gloriaberis in miserationibus illius.
text_el: ζῶν καὶ ὑγιὴς αἰνέσει τὸν κύριον

text_en: How great is the mercy of the Lord , and his forgiveness to them that turn to him!
text_la: Quam magna misericordia Domini, et propitiatio illius convertentibus ad se!
text_el: ὡς μεγάλη ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἐξιλασμὸς τοῖς ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπ' αὐτόν

text_en: For all things cannot be in men , because the son of man is not immortal , and they are delighted with the vanity of evil .
text_la: Nec enim omnia possunt esse in hominibus, quoniam non est immortalis filius hominis, et in vanitate malitiæ placuerunt.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ δύναται πάντα εἶναι ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὅτι οὐκ ἀθάνατος υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου

text_en: What is brighter than the sun; yet it shall be eclipsed. Or what is more wicked than that which flesh and blood has invented? And this shall be reproved.
text_la: Quid lucidius sole? et hic deficiet; aut quid nequius quam quod excogitavit caro et sanguis? et hoc arguetur.
text_el: τί φωτεινότερον ἡλίου καὶ τοῦτο ἐκλείπει καὶ πονηρὸν ἐνθυμηθήσεται σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα

text_en: He beholds the power of the height of heaven : and all men are earth and ashes.
text_la: Virtutem altitudinis cæli ipse conspicit : et omnes homines terra et cinis.
text_el: δύναμιν ὕψους οὐρανοῦ αὐτὸς ἐπισκέπτεται καὶ ἄνθρωποι πάντες γῆ καὶ σποδός

text_en: He that lives for ever created all things together. God only shall be justified, and he remains an invincible king for ever.
text_la: Qui vivet in æternum creavit omnia simul. Deus solus justificabitur, et manet invictus rex in æternum.
text_el: ὁ ζῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἔκτισεν τὰ πάντα κοινῇ κύριος μόνος δικαιωθήσεται

text_en: Who is able to declare his works?
text_la: Quis sufficit enarrare opera illius?
text_el: οὐθενὶ ἐξεποίησεν ἐξαγγεῖλαι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ

text_en: For who shall search out his glorious acts?
text_la: quis enim investigabit magnalia ejus?
text_el: καὶ τίς ἐξιχνεύσει τὰ μεγαλεῖα αὐτοῦ

text_en: And who shall show forth the power of his majesty? Or who shall be able to declare his mercy?
text_la: virtutem autem magnitudinis ejus quis enuntiabit? aut quis adjiciet enarrare misericordiam ejus?
text_el: κράτος μεγαλωσύνης αὐτοῦ τίς ἐξαριθμήσεται καὶ τίς προσθήσει ἐκδιηγήσασθαι τὰ ἐλέη αὐτοῦ

text_en: Nothing may be taken away, nor added, neither is it possible to find out the glorious works of God .
text_la: Non est minuere neque adjicere, nec est invenire magnalia Dei.
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλαττῶσαι οὐδὲ προσθεῖναι καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐξιχνιάσαι τὰ θαυμάσια τοῦ κυρίου

text_en: When a man has done, then shall he begin: and when he leaves off, he shall be at a loss.
text_la: Cum consummaverit homo, tunc incipiet : et cum quieverit, aporiabitur.
text_el: ὅταν συντελέσῃ ἄνθρωπος τότε ἄρχεται καὶ ὅταν παύσηται τότε ἀπορηθήσεται

text_en: What is man , and what is his grace ? And what is his good , or what is his evil ?
text_la: Quid est homo? et quæ est gratia illius? et quid bonum aut quid nequam illius?
text_el: τί ἄνθρωπος καὶ τί ἡ χρῆσις αὐτοῦ τί τὸ ἀγαθὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ τί τὸ κακὸν αὐτοῦ

text_en: The number of the days of men at the most are a hundred years, as a drop of water of the sea are they esteemed: and as a pebble of the sand, so are a few years compared to eternity .
text_la: Numerus dierum hominum, ut multum centum anni, quasi gutta aquæ maris deputati sunt : et sicut calculus arenæ, sic exigui anni in die ævi.
text_el: ἀριθμὸς ἡμερῶν ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ ἔτη ἑκατόν ὡς σταγὼν ὕδατος ἀπὸ θαλάσσης καὶ ψῆφος ἄμμου οὕτως ὀλίγα ἔτη ἐν ἡμέρᾳ αἰῶνος

text_en: Therefore God is patient in them, and pours forth his mercy upon them.
text_la: Propter hoc patiens est Deus in illis, et effundit super eos misericordiam suam.
text_el: διὰ τοῦτο ἐμακροθύμησεν κύριος ἐπ' αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐξέχεεν ἐπ' αὐτοὺς τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ

text_en: He has seen the presumption of their heart that it is wicked , and has known their end that it is evil .
text_la: Vidit præsumptionem cordis eorum, quoniam mala est : et cognovit subversionem illorum, quoniam nequam est.
text_el: εἶδεν καὶ ἐπέγνω τὴν καταστροφὴν αὐτῶν ὅτι πονηρά

text_en: Therefore has he filled up his mercy in their favour, and has shown them the way of justice .
text_la: Ideo adimplevit propitiationem suam in illis, et ostendit eis viam æquitatis.
text_el: διὰ τοῦτο ἐπλήθυνεν τὸν ἐξιλασμὸν αὐτοῦ

text_en: The compassion of man is toward his neighbour: but the mercy of God is upon all flesh.
text_la: Miseratio hominis circa proximum suum : misericordia autem Dei super omnem carnem.
text_el: ἔλεος ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τὸν πλησίον αὐτοῦ ἔλεος δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα

text_en: He has mercy, and teaches, and corrects, as a shepherd does his flock.
text_la: Qui misericordiam habet, docet et erudit quasi pastor gregem suum.
text_el: ἐλέγχων καὶ παιδεύων καὶ διδάσκων καὶ ἐπιστρέφων ὡς ποιμὴν τὸ ποίμνιον αὐτοῦ

text_en: He has mercy on him that receives the discipline of mercy, and that makes haste in his judgments.
text_la: Miseretur excipientis doctrinam miserationis, et qui festinat in judiciis ejus.
text_el: τοὺς ἐκδεχομένους παιδείαν ἐλεᾷ καὶ τοὺς κατασπεύδοντας ἐπὶ τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ

text_en: My son, in your good deeds , make no complaint, and when you give anything, add not grief by an evil word.
text_la: Fili, in bonis non des querelam, et in omni dato non des tristitiam verbi mali.
text_el: τέκνον ἐν ἀγαθοῖς μὴ δῷς μῶμον καὶ ἐν πάσῃ δόσει λύπην λόγων

text_en: Shall not the dew assuage the heat? So also the good word is better than the gift.
text_la: Nonne ardorem refrigerabit ros? sic et verbum melius quam datum.
text_el: οὐχὶ καύσωνα ἀναπαύσει δρόσος οὕτως κρείσσων λόγος ἢ δόσις

text_en: Lo, is not a word better than a gift? But both are with a justified man .
text_la: Nonne ecce verbum super datum bonum? sed utraque cum homine justificato.
text_el: οὐκ ἰδοὺ λόγος ὑπὲρ δόμα ἀγαθόν καὶ ἀμφότερα παρὰ ἀνδρὶ κεχαριτωμένῳ

text_en: A fool will upbraid bitterly: and a gift of one ill taught consumes the eyes.
text_la: Stultus acriter improperabit : et datus indisciplinati tabescere facit oculos.
text_el: μωρὸς ἀχαρίστως ὀνειδιεῖ καὶ δόσις βασκάνου ἐκτήκει ὀφθαλμούς

text_en: Before judgment prepare you justice , and learn before you speak.
text_la: Ante judicium para justitiam tibi, et antequam loquaris, disce.
text_el: πρὶν ἢ λαλῆσαι μάνθανε

text_en: Before sickness take a medicine, and before judgment examine yourself, and you shall find mercy in the sight of God .
text_la: Ante languorem adhibe medicinam : et ante judicium interroga teipsum, et in conspectu Dei invenies propitiationem.
text_el: καὶ πρὸ ἀρρωστίας θεραπεύου πρὸ κρίσεως ἐξέταζε σεαυτόν καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς εὑρήσεις ἐξιλασμόν

text_en: Humble yourself before you are sick, and in the time of sickness show your conversation.
text_la: Ante languorem humilia te, et in tempore infirmitatis ostende conversationem tuam.
text_el: πρὶν ἀρρωστῆσαί σε ταπεινώθητι καὶ ἐν καιρῷ ἁμαρτημάτων δεῖξον ἐπιστροφήν

text_en: Let nothing hinder you from praying always, and be not afraid to be justified even to death: for the reward of God continues for ever.
text_la: Non impediaris orare semper, et ne verearis usque ad mortem justificari, quoniam merces Dei manet in æternum.
text_el: μὴ ἐμποδισθῇς τοῦ ἀποδοῦναι εὐχὴν εὐκαίρως καὶ μὴ μείνῃς ἕως θανάτου δικαιωθῆναι

text_en: Before prayer prepare your soul : and be not as a man that tempts God .
text_la: Ante orationem præpara animam tuam, et noli esse quasi homo qui tentat Deum.
text_el: πρὶν εὔξασθαι ἑτοίμασον σεαυτὸν καὶ μὴ γίνου ὡς ἄνθρωπος πειράζων τὸν κύριον

text_en: Remember the wrath that shall be at the last day, and the time of repaying when he shall turn away his face.
text_la: Memento iræ in die consummationis, et tempus retributionis in conversatione faciei.
text_el: μνήσθητι θυμοῦ ἐν ἡμέραις τελευτῆς καὶ καιρὸν ἐκδικήσεως ἐν ἀποστροφῇ προσώπου

text_en: Remember poverty in the time of abundance, and the necessities of poverty in the day of riches.
text_la: Memento paupertatis in tempore abundantiæ, et necessitatum paupertatis in die divitiarum.
text_el: μνήσθητι καιρὸν λιμοῦ ἐν καιρῷ πλησμονῆς πτωχείαν καὶ ἔνδειαν ἐν ἡμέραις πλούτου

text_en: From the morning until the evening the time shall be changed, and all these are swift in the eyes of God .
text_la: A mane usque ad vesperam immutabitur tempus, et hæc omnia citata in oculis Dei.
text_el: ἀπὸ πρωίθεν ἕως ἑσπέρας μεταβάλλει καιρός καὶ πάντα ἐστὶν ταχινὰ ἔναντι κυρίου

text_en: A wise man will fear in everything, and in the days of sins will beware of sloth .
text_la: Homo sapiens in omnibus metuet, et in diebus delictorum attendet ab inertia.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος σοφὸς ἐν παντὶ εὐλαβηθήσεται καὶ ἐν ἡμέραις ἁμαρτιῶν προσέξει ἀπὸ πλημμελείας

text_en: Every man of understanding knows wisdom, and will give praise to him that finds her.
text_la: Omnis astutus agnoscit sapientiam, et invenienti eam dabit confessionem.
text_el: πᾶς συνετὸς ἔγνω σοφίαν καὶ τῷ εὑρόντι αὐτὴν δώσει ἐξομολόγησιν

text_en: They that were of good understanding in words, have also done wisely themselves: and have understood truth and justice , and have poured forth proverbs and judgments.
text_la: Sensati in verbis et ipsi sapienter egerunt, et intellexerunt veritatem et justitiam, et impleverunt proverbia et judicia.
text_el: συνετοὶ ἐν λόγοις καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσοφίσαντο καὶ ἀνώμβρησαν παροιμίας ἀκριβεῖς

text_en: Go not after your lusts , but turn away from your own will.
text_la: Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere.
text_el: ὀπίσω τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν σου μὴ πορεύου καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀρέξεών σου κωλύου

text_en: If you give to your soul her desires, she will make you a joy to your enemies.
text_la: Si præstes animæ tuæ concupiscentias ejus, faciat te in gaudium inimicis tuis.
text_el: ἐὰν χορηγήσῃς τῇ ψυχῇ σου εὐδοκίαν ἐπιθυμίας ποιήσει σε ἐπίχαρμα τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου

text_en: Take no pleasure in riotous assemblies, be they ever so small: for their concertation is continual.
text_la: Ne oblecteris in turbis nec in modicis : assidua enim est commissio illorum.
text_el: μὴ εὐφραίνου ἐπὶ πολλῇ τρυφῇ μὴ προσδεθῇς συμβολῇ αὐτῆς

text_en: Make not yourself poor by borrowing to contribute to feasts when you have nothing in your purse: for you shall be an enemy to your own life.
text_la: Ne fueris mediocris in contentione ex fœnore, et est tibi nihil in sacculo : eris enim invidus vitæ tuæ.
text_el: μὴ γίνου πτωχὸς συμβολοκοπῶν ἐκ δανεισμοῦ καὶ οὐδέν σοί ἐστιν ἐν μαρσιππίῳ

text_en: A workman that is a drunkard shall not be rich: and he that contemns small things, shall fall by little and little.
text_la: Operarius ebriosus non locupletabitur : et qui spernit modica paulatim decidet.
text_el: ἐργάτης μέθυσος οὐ πλουτισθήσεται ὁ ἐξουθενῶν τὰ ὀλίγα κατὰ μικρὸν πεσεῖται

text_en: Wine and women make wise men fall off, and shall rebuke the prudent :
text_la: Vinum et mulieres apostatare faciunt sapientes, et arguent sensatos.
text_el: οἶνος καὶ γυναῖκες ἀποστήσουσιν συνετούς

text_en: And he that joins himself to harlots, will be wicked . Rottenness and worms shall inherit him, and he shall be lifted up for a greater example, and his soul shall be taken away out of the number.
text_la: Et qui se jungit fornicariis erit nequam : putredo et vermes hæreditabunt illum : et extolletur in exemplum majus, et tolletur de numero anima ejus.
text_el: καὶ ὁ κολλώμενος πόρναις τολμηρότερος ἔσται σήπη καὶ σκώληκες κληρονομήσουσιν αὐτόν καὶ ψυχὴ τολμηρὰ ἐξαρθήσεται

text_en: He that is hasty to give credit, is light of heart, and shall be lessened: and he that sins against his own soul , shall be despised .
text_la: Qui credit cito levis corde est, et minorabitur : et qui delinquit in animam suam, insuper habebitur.
text_el: ὁ ταχὺ ἐμπιστεύων κοῦφος καρδίᾳ καὶ ὁ ἁμαρτάνων εἰς ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ πλημμελήσει

text_en: He that rejoices in iniquity , shall be censured, and he that hates chastisement, shall have less life: and he that hates babbling, extinguishes evil .
text_la: Qui gaudet iniquitate, denotabitur : et qui odit correptionem, minuetur vita : et qui odit loquacitatem, extinguit malitiam.

text_en: He that sins against his own soul , shall repent: and he that is delighted with wickedness , shall be condemned.
text_la: Qui peccat in animam suam, pœnitebit : et qui jucundatur in malitia, denotabitur.
text_el: ὁ εὐφραινόμενος καρδίᾳ καταγνωσθήσεται καὶ ὁ μισῶν λαλιὰν ἐλαττονοῦται κακίᾳ

text_en: Rehearse not again a wicked and harsh word, and you shall not fare the worse.
text_la: Ne iteres verbum nequam et durum, et non minoraberis.
text_el: μηδέποτε δευτερώσῃς λόγον καὶ οὐθέν σοι οὐ μὴ ἐλαττονωθῇ

text_en: Tell not your mind to friend or foe: and if there be a sin with you, disclose it not.
text_la: Amico et inimico noli narrare sensum tuum : et si est tibi delictum, noli denudare :
text_el: ἐν φίλῳ καὶ ἐχθρῷ μὴ διηγοῦ καὶ εἰ μή ἐστίν σοι ἁμαρτία μὴ ἀποκάλυπτε

text_en: For he will hearken to you, and will watch you, and as it were defending your sin he will hate you, and so will he be with you always.
text_la: audiet enim te, et custodiet te, et quasi defendens peccatum, odiet te, et sic aderit tibi semper.
text_el: ἀκήκοεν γάρ σου καὶ ἐφυλάξατό σε καὶ ἐν καιρῷ μισήσει σε

text_en: Have you heard a word against your neighbour? Let it die within you, trusting that it will not burst you.
text_la: Audisti verbum adversus proximum tuum? commoriatur in te, fidens quoniam non te dirumpet.
text_el: ἀκήκοας λόγον συναποθανέτω σοι θάρσει οὐ μή σε ῥήξει

text_en: At the hearing of a word the fool is in travail, as a woman groaning in the bringing forth a child.
text_la: A facie verbi parturit fatuus, tamquam gemitus partus infantis.
text_el: ἀπὸ προσώπου λόγου ὠδινήσει μωρὸς ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου βρέφους ἡ τίκτουσα

text_en: As an arrow that sticks in a man's thigh: so is a word in the heart of a fool.
text_la: Sagitta infixa femori carnis, sic verbum in corde stulti.
text_el: βέλος πεπηγὸς ἐν μηρῷ σαρκός οὕτως λόγος ἐν κοιλίᾳ μωροῦ

text_en: Reprove a friend, lest he may not have understood, and say: I did it not: or if he did it, that he may do it no more.
text_la: Corripe amicum, ne forte non intellexerit, et dicat : Non feci : aut, si fecerit, ne iterum addat facere.
text_el: ἔλεγξον φίλον μήποτε οὐκ ἐποίησεν καὶ εἴ τι ἐποίησεν μήποτε προσθῇ

text_en: Reprove your neighbour, for it may be he has not said it: and if he has said it, that he may not say it again.
text_la: Corripe proximum, ne forte non dixerit : et si dixerit, ne forte iteret.
text_el: ἔλεγξον τὸν πλησίον μήποτε οὐκ εἶπεν καὶ εἰ εἴρηκεν ἵνα μὴ δευτερώσῃ

text_en: Admonish your friend: for there is often a fault committed.
text_la: Corripe amicum, sæpe enim fit commissio :
text_el: ἔλεγξον φίλον πολλάκις γὰρ γίνεται διαβολή

text_en: And believe not every word. There is one, that slips with the tongue, but not from his heart.
text_la: et non omni verbo credas. Est qui labitur lingua, sed non ex animo :
text_el: καὶ μὴ παντὶ λόγῳ πίστευε ἔστιν ὀλισθάνων καὶ οὐκ ἀπὸ ψυχῆς

text_en: For who is there that has not offended with his tongue? Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him.
text_la: quis est enim qui non deliquerit in lingua sua? Corripe proximum antequam commineris,
text_el: καὶ τίς οὐχ ἥμαρτεν ἐν τῇ γλώσσῃ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγξον τὸν πλησίον σου πρὶν ἢ ἀπειλῆσαι

text_en: And give place to the fear of the most High : for the fear of God is all wisdom, and therein is to fear God , and the disposition of the law is in all wisdom.
text_la: et da locum timori Altissimi : quia omnis sapientia timor Dei, et in illa timere Deum, et in omni sapientia dispositio legis.
text_el: καὶ δὸς τόπον νόμῳ ὑψίστου πᾶσα σοφία φόβος κυρίου καὶ ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ ποίησις νόμου

text_en: But the learning of wickedness is not wisdom: and the device of sinners is not prudence .
text_la: Et non est sapientia nequitiæ disciplina, et non est cogitatus peccatorum prudentia.
text_el: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν σοφία πονηρίας ἐπιστήμη καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπου βουλὴ ἁμαρτωλῶν φρόνησις

text_en: There is a subtle wickedness , and the same is detestable: and there is a man that is foolish, wanting in wisdom.
text_la: Est nequitia, et in ipsa execratio, et est insipiens qui minuitur sapientia.
text_el: ἔστιν πανουργία καὶ αὕτη βδέλυγμα καὶ ἔστιν ἄφρων ἐλαττούμενος σοφίᾳ

text_en: Better is a man that has less wisdom, and wants understanding, with the fear of God , than he that abounds in understanding, and transgresses the law of the most High .
text_la: Melior est homo qui minuitur sapientia, et deficiens sensu, in timore, quam qui abundat sensu, et transgreditur legem Altissimi.
text_el: κρείττων ἡττώμενος ἐν συνέσει ἔμφοβος ἢ περισσεύων ἐν φρονήσει καὶ παραβαίνων νόμον

text_en: There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust .
text_la: Est solertia certa, et ipsa iniqua :
text_el: ἔστιν πανουργία ἀκριβὴς καὶ αὕτη ἄδικος

text_en: And there is one that utters an exact word telling the truth . There is one that humbles himself wickedly , and his interior is full of deceit :
text_la: et est qui emittit verbum certum enarrans veritatem. Est qui nequiter humiliat se, et interiora ejus plena sunt dolo :
text_el: καὶ ἔστιν διαστρέφων χάριν τοῦ ἐκφᾶναι κρίμα ἔστιν πονηρευόμενος συγκεκυφὼς μελανίᾳ καὶ τὰ ἐντὸς αὐτοῦ πλήρη δόλου

text_en: And there is one that submits himself exceedingly with a great lowliness: and there is one that casts down his countenance, and makes as if he did not see that which is unknown:
text_la: et est qui se nimium submittit a multa humilitate : et est qui inclinat faciem suam, et fingit se non videre quod ignoratum est :
text_el: συγκρύφων πρόσωπον καὶ ἐθελοκωφῶν ὅπου οὐκ ἐπεγνώσθη προφθάσει σε

text_en: And if he be hindered from sinning for want of power, if he shall find opportunity to do evil , he will do it.
text_la: et si ab imbecillitate virium vetetur peccare, si invenerit tempus malefaciendi, malefaciet.
text_el: καὶ ἐὰν ὑπὸ ἐλαττώματος ἰσχύος κωλυθῇ ἁμαρτεῖν ἐὰν εὕρῃ καιρόν κακοποιήσει

text_en: A man is known by his look, and a wise man , when you meet him, is known by his countenance.
text_la: Ex visu cognoscitur vir, et ab occursu faciei cognoscitur sensatus.
text_el: ἀπὸ ὁράσεως ἐπιγνωσθήσεται ἀνήρ καὶ ἀπὸ ἀπαντήσεως προσώπου ἐπιγνωσθήσεται νοήμων

text_en: The attire of the body, and the laughter of the teeth, and the gait of the man , show what he is.
text_la: Amictus corporis, et risus dentium, et ingressus hominis, enuntiant de illo.
text_el: στολισμὸς ἀνδρὸς καὶ γέλως ὀδόντων καὶ βήματα ἀνθρώπου ἀναγγελεῖ τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ

text_en: There is a lying rebuke in the anger of an injurious man : and there is a judgment that is not allowed to be good : and there is one that holds his peace, he is wise.
text_la: Est correptio mendax in ira contumeliosi, et est judicium quod non probatur esse bonum : et est tacens, et ipse est prudens.
text_el: ἔστιν ἔλεγχος ὃς οὐκ ἔστιν ὡραῖος καὶ ἔστιν σιωπῶν καὶ αὐτὸς φρόνιμος

text_en: How much better is it to reprove, than to be angry , and not to hinder him that confesses in prayer .
text_la: Quam bonum est arguere, quam irasci, et confitentem in oratione non prohibere!
text_el: ὡς καλὸν ἐλέγξαι ἢ θυμοῦσθαι καὶ ὁ ἀνθομολογούμενος ἀπὸ ἐλαττώσεως κωλυθήσεται

text_en: The lust of an eunuch shall deflour a young maiden:
text_la: Concupiscentia spadonis devirginabit juvenculam :
text_el: ἐπιθυμία εὐνούχου ἀποπαρθενῶσαι νεάνιδα

text_en: So is he that by violence executes of the unwise.
text_la: sic qui facit per vim judicium iniquum.
text_el: οὕτως ὁ ποιῶν ἐν βίᾳ κρίματα

text_en: How good is it, when you are reproved, to show repentance! for so you shall escape wilful sin .
text_la: Quam bonum est correptum manifestare pœnitentiam! sic enim effugies voluntarium peccatum.

text_en: There is one that holds his peace, that is found wise: and there is another that is hateful , that is bold in speech.
text_la: Est tacens qui invenitur sapiens : et est odibilis qui procax est ad loquendum.
text_el: ἔστιν σιωπῶν εὑρισκόμενος σοφός καὶ ἔστιν μισητὸς ἀπὸ πολλῆς λαλιᾶς

text_en: There is one that holds his peace, because he knows not what to say: and there is another that holds his peace, knowing the proper time.
text_la: Est tacens non habens sensum loquelæ : et est tacens sciens tempus aptum.
text_el: ἔστιν σιωπῶν οὐ γὰρ ἔχει ἀπόκρισιν καὶ ἔστιν σιωπῶν εἰδὼς καιρόν

text_en: A wise man will hold his peace till he see opportunity: but a babbler, and a fool, will regard no time.
text_la: Homo sapiens tacebit usque ad tempus : lascivus autem et imprudens non servabunt tempus.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος σοφὸς σιγήσει ἕως καιροῦ ὁ δὲ λαπιστὴς καὶ ἄφρων ὑπερβήσεται καιρόν

text_en: He that uses many words shall hurt his own soul : and he that takes authority to himself unjustly shall be hated .
text_la: Qui multis utitur verbis lædet animam suam : et qui potestatem sibi sumit injuste, odietur.
text_el: ὁ πλεονάζων λόγῳ βδελυχθήσεται καὶ ὁ ἐνεξουσιαζόμενος μισηθήσεται

text_en: There is success in evil things to a man without discipline, and there is a finding that turns to loss.
text_la: Est processio in malis viro indisciplinato, et est inventio in detrimentum.
text_el: ἔστιν εὐοδία ἐν κακοῖς ἀνδρί καὶ ἔστιν εὕρεμα εἰς ἐλάττωσιν

text_en: There is a gift that is not profitable: and there is a gift, the recompense of which is double.
text_la: Est datum quod non est utile, et est datum cujus retributio duplex.
text_el: ἔστιν δόσις ἣ οὐ λυσιτελήσει σοι καὶ ἔστιν δόσις ἧς τὸ ἀνταπόδομα διπλοῦν

text_en: There is an abasement because of glory : and there is one that shall lift up his head from a low estate.
text_la: Est propter gloriam minoratio, et est qui ab humilitate levabit caput.
text_el: ἔστιν ἐλάττωσις ἕνεκεν δόξης καὶ ἔστιν ὃς ἀπὸ ταπεινώσεως ἦρεν κεφαλήν

text_en: There is that buys much for a small price, and restores the same sevenfold.
text_la: Est qui multa redimat modico pretio, et restituens ea in septuplum.
text_el: ἔστιν ἀγοράζων πολλὰ ὀλίγου καὶ ἀποτιννύων αὐτὰ ἑπταπλάσιον

text_en: A man wise in words shall make himself beloved: but the graces of fools shall be poured out.
text_la: Sapiens in verbis seipsum amabilem facit : gratiæ autem fatuorum effundentur.
text_el: ὁ σοφὸς ἐν λόγοις ἑαυτὸν προσφιλῆ ποιήσει χάριτες δὲ μωρῶν ἐκχυθήσονται

text_en: The gift of the fool shall do you no good : for his eyes are sevenfold.
text_la: Datus insipientis non erit utilis tibi : oculi enim illius septemplices sunt.
text_el: δόσις ἄφρονος οὐ λυσιτελήσει σοι οἱ γὰρ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ἀνθ' ἑνὸς πολλοί

text_en: He will give a few things, and upbraid much: and the opening of his mouth is the kindling of a fire.
text_la: Exigua dabit, et multa improperabit : et apertio oris illius inflammatio est.
text_el: ὀλίγα δώσει καὶ πολλὰ ὀνειδίσει καὶ ἀνοίξει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ὡς κῆρυξ

text_en: Today a man lends, and tomorrow he asks it again: such a man as this is hateful .
text_la: Hodie fœneratur quis, et cras expetit : odibilis est homo hujusmodi.
text_el: σήμερον δανιεῖ καὶ αὔριον ἀπαιτήσει μισητὸς ἄνθρωπος ὁ τοιοῦτος

text_en: A fool shall have no friend, and there shall be no thanks for his good deeds .
text_la: Fatuo non erit amicus, et non erit gratia bonis illius :
text_el: μωρὸς ἐρεῖ οὐχ ὑπάρχει μοι φίλος καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν χάρις τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς μου

text_en: For they that eat his bread, are of a false tongue. How often, and how many will laugh him to scorn!
text_la: qui enim edunt panem illius, falsæ linguæ sunt. Quoties et quanti irridebunt eum!
text_el: οἱ ἔσθοντες τὸν ἄρτον αὐτοῦ φαῦλοι γλώσσῃ ποσάκις καὶ ὅσοι καταγελάσονται αὐτοῦ

text_en: For he does not distribute with right understanding that which was to be had: in like manner also that which was not to be had.
text_la: neque enim quod habendum erat directo sensu distribuit; similiter et quod non erat habendum.

text_en: The slipping of a false tongue is as one that falls on the pavement: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.
text_la: Lapsus falsæ linguæ quasi qui in pavimento cadens : sic casus malorum festinanter veniet.
text_el: ὀλίσθημα ἀπὸ ἐδάφους μᾶλλον ἢ ἀπὸ γλώσσης οὕτως πτῶσις κακῶν κατὰ σπουδὴν ἥξει

text_en: A man without grace is as a vain fable, it shall be continually in the mouth of the unwise.
text_la: Homo acharis quasi fabula vana, in ore indisciplinatorum assidua erit.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος ἄχαρις μῦθος ἄκαιρος ἐν στόματι ἀπαιδεύτων ἐνδελεχισθήσεται

text_en: A parable coming out of a fool's mouth shall be rejected: for he does not speak it in due season.
text_la: Ex ore fatui reprobabitur parabola : non enim dicit illam in tempore suo.
text_el: ἀπὸ στόματος μωροῦ ἀποδοκιμασθήσεται παραβολή οὐ γὰρ μὴ εἴπῃ αὐτὴν ἐν καιρῷ αὐτῆς

text_en: There is that is hindered from sinning through want, and in his rest he shall be pricked.
text_la: Est qui vetatur peccare præ inopia, et in requie sua stimulabitur.
text_el: ἔστιν κωλυόμενος ἁμαρτάνειν ἀπὸ ἐνδείας καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀναπαύσει αὐτοῦ οὐ κατανυγήσεται

text_en: There is that will destroy his own soul through shamefacedness, and by occasion of an unwise person he will destroy it: and by respect of person he will destroy himself.
text_la: Est qui perdet animam suam præ confusione, et ab imprudenti persona perdet eam : personæ autem acceptione perdet se.
text_el: ἔστιν ἀπολλύων τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ δι' αἰσχύνην καὶ ἀπὸ ἄφρονος προσώπου ἀπολεῖ αὐτήν

text_en: There is that for bashfulness promises to his friend, and makes him his enemy for nothing.
text_la: Est qui præ confusione promittit amico, et lucratus est eum inimicum gratis.
text_el: ἔστιν χάριν αἰσχύνης ἐπαγγελλόμενος φίλῳ καὶ ἐκτήσατο αὐτὸν ἐχθρὸν δωρεάν

text_en: A lie is a foul blot in a man , and yet it will be continually in the mouth of men without discipline.
text_la: Opprobrium nequam in homine mendacium : et in ore indisciplinatorum assidue erit.
text_el: μῶμος πονηρὸς ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ ψεῦδος ἐν στόματι ἀπαιδεύτων ἐνδελεχισθήσεται

text_en: A thief is better than a man that is always lying: but both of them shall inherit destruction.
text_la: Potior fur quam assiduitas viri mendacis : perditionem autem ambo hæreditabunt.
text_el: αἱρετὸν κλέπτης ἢ ὁ ἐνδελεχίζων ψεύδει ἀμφότεροι δὲ ἀπώλειαν κληρονομήσουσιν

text_en: The manners of lying men are without honour : and their confusion is with them without ceasing.
text_la: Mores hominum mendacium sine honore, et confusio illorum cum ipsis sine intermissione.
text_el: ἦθος ἀνθρώπου ψευδοῦς ἀτιμία καὶ ἡ αἰσχύνη αὐτοῦ μετ' αὐτοῦ ἐνδελεχῶς

text_en: A wise man shall advance himself with his words, and a prudent man shall please the great ones.
text_la: Sapiens in verbis producet seipsum, et homo prudens placebit magnatis.
text_el: ὁ σοφὸς ἐν λόγοις προάξει ἑαυτόν καὶ ἄνθρωπος φρόνιμος ἀρέσει μεγιστᾶσιν

text_en: He that tills his land shall make a high heap of corn: and he that works justice shall be exalted: and he that pleases great men shall escape iniquity .
text_la: Qui operatur terram suam inaltabit acervum frugum, et qui operatur justitiam, ipse exaltabitur : qui vero placet magnatis effugiet iniquitatem.
text_el: ὁ ἐργαζόμενος γῆν ἀνυψώσει θιμωνιὰν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ ἀρέσκων μεγιστᾶσιν ἐξιλάσεται ἀδικίαν

text_en: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of judges, and make them dumb in the mouth, so that they cannot correct.
text_la: Xenia et dona excæcant oculos judicum, et quasi mutus, in ore avertit correptiones eorum.
text_el: ξένια καὶ δῶρα ἀποτυφλοῖ ὀφθαλμοὺς σοφῶν καὶ ὡς φιμὸς ἐν στόματι ἀποτρέπει ἐλεγμούς

text_en: O Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is not seen: what profit is there in them both?
text_la: Sapientia absconsa, et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?
text_el: σοφία κεκρυμμένη καὶ θησαυρὸς ἀφανής τίς ὠφέλεια ἐν ἀμφοτέροις

text_en: Better is he that hides his folly, than the man that hides his wisdom.
text_la: Melior est qui celat insipientiam suam, quam homo qui abscondit sapientiam suam.
text_el: κρείσσων ἄνθρωπος ἀποκρύπτων τὴν μωρίαν αὐτοῦ ἢ ἄνθρωπος ἀποκρύπτων τὴν σοφίαν αὐτοῦ

text_en: My son, have you sinned ? Do so no more: but for your former sins also pray that they may be forgiven you.
text_la: Fili, peccasti, non adjicias iterum : sed et de pristinis deprecare, ut tibi dimittantur.
text_el: τέκνον ἥμαρτες μὴ προσθῇς μηκέτι καὶ περὶ τῶν προτέρων σου δεήθητι

text_en: Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent: for if you come near them, they will take hold of you.
text_la: Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccata : et si accesseris ad illa, suscipient te.
text_el: ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου ὄφεως φεῦγε ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας ἐὰν γὰρ προσέλθῃς δήξεταί σε

text_en: The teeth thereof are the teeth of a lion, killing the souls of men .
text_la: Dentes leonis dentes ejus, interficientes animas hominum.
text_el: ὀδόντες λέοντος οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτῆς ἀναιροῦντες ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων

text_en: All iniquity is like a two-edged sword, there is no remedy for the wound thereof.
text_la: Quasi rhomphæa bis acuta omnis iniquitas : plagæ illius non est sanitas.
text_el: ὡς ῥομφαία δίστομος πᾶσα ἀνομία τῇ πληγῇ αὐτῆς οὐκ ἔστιν ἴασις

text_en: Injuries and wrongs will waste riches: and the house that is very rich shall be brought to nothing by pride : so the substance of the proud shall be rooted out.
text_la: Objurgatio et injuriæ annullabunt substantiam, et domus quæ nimis locuples est annullabitur superbia : sic substantia superbi eradicabitur.
text_el: καταπληγμὸς καὶ ὕβρις ἐρημώσουσιν πλοῦτον οὕτως οἶκος ὑπερηφάνου ἐρημωθήσεται

text_en: The prayer out of the mouth of the poor shall reach the ears of God , and judgment shall come for him speedily.
text_la: Deprecatio pauperis ex ore usque ad aures ejus perveniet, et judicium festinato adveniet illi.
text_el: δέησις πτωχοῦ ἐκ στόματος ἕως ὠτίων αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ κρίμα αὐτοῦ κατὰ σπουδὴν ἔρχεται

text_en: He that hates to be reproved walks in the trace of a sinner: and he that fears God will turn to his own heart.
text_la: Qui odit correptionem vestigium est peccatoris, et qui timet Deum convertetur ad cor suum.
text_el: μισῶν ἐλεγμὸν ἐν ἴχνει ἁμαρτωλοῦ καὶ ὁ φοβούμενος κύριον ἐπιστρέψει ἐν καρδίᾳ

text_en: He that is mighty by a bold tongue is known afar off, but a wise man knows to slip by him.
text_la: Notus a longe potens lingua audaci, et sensatus scit labi se ab ipso.
text_el: γνωστὸς μακρόθεν ὁ δυνατὸς ἐν γλώσσῃ ὁ δὲ νοήμων οἶδεν ἐν τῷ ὀλισθάνειν αὐτόν

text_en: He that builds his house at other men's charges, is as he that gathers himself stones to build in the winter.
text_la: Qui ædificat domum suam impendiis alienis, quasi qui colligat lapides suos in hieme.
text_el: ὁ οἰκοδομῶν τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ ἐν χρήμασιν ἀλλοτρίοις ὡς συνάγων αὐτοῦ τοὺς λίθους εἰς χειμῶνα

text_en: The congregation of sinners is like tow heaped together, and the end of them is a flame of fire.
text_la: Stupa collecta synagoga peccantium, et consummatio illorum flamma ignis.
text_el: στιππύον συνηγμένον συναγωγὴ ἀνόμων καὶ ἡ συντέλεια αὐτῶν φλὸξ πυρός

text_en: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, and in their end is hell, and darkness, and pains.
text_la: Via peccatorum complanata lapidibus : et in fine illorum inferi, et tenebræ, et pœnæ.
text_el: ὁδὸς ἁμαρτωλῶν ὡμαλισμένη ἐκ λίθων καὶ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων αὐτῆς βόθρος ᾅδου

text_en: He that keeps justice shall get the understanding thereof.
text_la: Qui custodit justitiam, continebit sensum ejus.
text_el: ὁ φυλάσσων νόμον κατακρατεῖ τοῦ ἐννοήματος αὐτοῦ

text_en: The perfection of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding.
text_la: Consummatio timoris Dei, sapientia et sensus.
text_el: καὶ συντέλεια τοῦ φόβου κυρίου σοφία

text_en: He that is not wise in good , will not be taught.
text_la: Non erudietur qui non est sapiens in bono.
text_el: οὐ παιδευθήσεται ὃς οὐκ ἔστιν πανοῦργος

text_en: But there is a wisdom that abounds in evil : and there is no understanding where there is bitterness.
text_la: Est autem sapientia quæ abundat in malo, et non est sensus ubi est amaritudo.
text_el: ἔστιν δὲ πανουργία πληθύνουσα πικρίαν

text_en: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood, and his counsel continues like a fountain of life.
text_la: Scientia sapientis tamquam inundatio abundabit, et consilium illius sicut fons vitæ permanet.
text_el: γνῶσις σοφοῦ ὡς κατακλυσμὸς πληθυνθήσεται καὶ ἡ βουλὴ αὐτοῦ ὡς πηγὴ ζωῆς

text_en: The heart of a fool is like a broken vessel, and no wisdom at all shall it hold.
text_la: Cor fatui quasi vas confractum, et omnem sapientiam non tenebit.
text_el: ἔγκατα μωροῦ ὡς ἀγγεῖον συντετριμμένον καὶ πᾶσαν γνῶσιν οὐ κρατήσει

text_en: A man of sense will praise every wise word he shall hear, and will apply it to himself: the luxurious man has heard it, and it shall displease him, and he will cast it behind his back.
text_la: Verbum sapiens quodcumque audierit scius, laudabit, et ad se adjiciet : audivit luxuriosus, et displicebit illi, et projiciet illud post dorsum suum.
text_el: λόγον σοφὸν ἐὰν ἀκούσῃ ἐπιστήμων αἰνέσει αὐτὸν καὶ ἐπ' αὐτὸν προσθήσει ἤκουσεν ὁ σπαταλῶν καὶ ἀπήρεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἀπέστρεψεν αὐτὸν ὀπίσω τοῦ νώτου αὐτοῦ

text_en: The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way: but in the lips of the wise, grace shall be found.
text_la: Narratio fatui quasi sarcina in via : nam in labiis sensati invenietur gratia.
text_el: ἐξήγησις μωροῦ ὡς ἐν ὁδῷ φορτίον ἐπὶ δὲ χείλους συνετοῦ εὑρεθήσεται χάρις

text_en: The mouth of the prudent is sought after in the church, and they will think upon his words in their hearts.
text_la: Os prudentis quæritur in ecclesia, et verba illius cogitabunt in cordibus suis.
text_el: στόμα φρονίμου ζητηθήσεται ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ διανοηθήσονται ἐν καρδίᾳ

text_en: As a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool: and the knowledge of the unwise is as words without sense.
text_la: Tamquam domus exterminata, sic fatuo sapientia : et scientia insensati inenarrabilia verba.
text_el: ὡς οἶκος ἠφανισμένος οὕτως μωρῷ σοφία καὶ γνῶσις ἀσυνέτου ἀδιεξέταστοι λόγοι

text_en: Doctrine to a fool is as fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand.
text_la: Compedes in pedibus, stulto doctrina : et quasi vincula manuum super manum dextram.
text_el: πέδαι ἐν ποσὶν ἀνοήτου παιδεία καὶ ὡς χειροπέδαι ἐπὶ χειρὸς δεξιᾶς

text_en: A fool lifts up his voice in laughter: but a wise man will scarce laugh low to himself.
text_la: Fatuus in risu exaltat vocem suam : vir autem sapiens vix tacite ridebit.
text_el: μωρὸς ἐν γέλωτι ἀνυψοῖ φωνὴν αὐτοῦ ἀνὴρ δὲ πανοῦργος μόλις ἡσυχῇ μειδιάσει

text_en: Learning to the prudent is as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arm.
text_la: Ornamentum aureum prudenti doctrina, et quasi brachiale in brachio dextro.
text_el: ὡς κόσμος χρυσοῦς φρονίμῳ παιδεία καὶ ὡς χλιδὼν ἐπὶ βραχίονι δεξιῷ

text_en: The foot of a fool is soon in his neighbour's house: but a man of experience will be abashed at the person of the mighty.
text_la: Pes fatui facilis in domum proximi : et homo peritus confundetur a persona potentis.
text_el: ποὺς μωροῦ ταχὺς εἰς οἰκίαν ἄνθρωπος δὲ πολύπειρος αἰσχυνθήσεται ἀπὸ προσώπου

text_en: A fool will peep through the window into the house: but he that is well taught will stand without.
text_la: Stultus a fenestra respiciet in domum : vir autem eruditus foris stabit.
text_el: ἄφρων ἀπὸ θύρας παρακύπτει εἰς οἰκίαν ἀνὴρ δὲ πεπαιδευμένος ἔξω στήσεται

text_en: It is the folly of a man to hearken at the door: and a wise man will be grieved with the disgrace.
text_la: Stultitia hominis auscultare per ostium : et prudens gravabitur contumelia.
text_el: ἀπαιδευσία ἀνθρώπου ἀκροᾶσθαι παρὰ θύραν ὁ δὲ φρόνιμος βαρυνθήσεται ἀτιμίᾳ

text_en: The lips of the unwise will be telling foolish things: but the words of the wise shall be weighed in a balance.
text_la: Labia imprudentium stulta narrabunt; verba autem prudentium statera ponderabuntur.
text_el: χείλη ἀλλοτρίων ἐν τούτοις διηγήσονται λόγοι δὲ φρονίμων ἐν ζυγῷ σταθήσονται

text_en: The heart of fools is in their mouth: and the mouth of wise men is in their heart.
text_la: In ore fatuorum cor illorum, et in corde sapientium os illorum.
text_el: ἐν στόματι μωρῶν ἡ καρδία αὐτῶν καρδία δὲ σοφῶν στόμα αὐτῶν

text_en: While the ungodly curses the devil , he curses his own soul .
text_la: Dum maledicit impius diabolum, maledicit ipse animam suam.
text_el: ἐν τῷ καταρᾶσθαι ἀσεβῆ τὸν σατανᾶν αὐτὸς καταρᾶται τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν

text_en: The talebearer shall defile his own soul , and shall be hated by all: and he that shall abide with him shall be hateful : the silent and wise man shall be honoured .
text_la: Susurro coinquinabit animam suam, et in omnibus odietur, et qui cum eo manserit odiosus erit : tacitus et sensatus honorabitur.
text_el: μολύνει τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν ὁ ψιθυρίζων καὶ ἐν παροικήσει μισηθήσεται

text_en: The sluggard is pelted with a dirty stone, and all men will speak of his disgrace.
text_la: In lapide luteo lapidatus est piger : et omnes loquentur super aspernationem illius.
text_el: λίθῳ ἠρδαλωμένῳ συνεβλήθη ὀκνηρός καὶ πᾶς ἐκσυριεῖ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀτιμίᾳ αὐτοῦ

text_en: The sluggard is pelted with the dung of oxen: and every one that touches him will shake his hands.
text_la: De stercore boum lapidatus est piger : et omnis qui tetigerit eum excutiet manus.
text_el: βολβίτῳ κοπρίων συνεβλήθη ὀκνηρός πᾶς ὁ ἀναιρούμενος αὐτὸν ἐκτινάξει χεῖρα

text_en: A son ill taught is the confusion of the father: and a foolish daughter shall be to his loss.
text_la: Confusio patris est de filio indisciplinato : filia autem in deminoratione fiet.
text_el: αἰσχύνη πατρὸς ἐν γεννήσει ἀπαιδεύτου θυγάτηρ δὲ ἐπ' ἐλαττώσει γίνεται

text_en: A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but she that confounds, becomes a disgrace to her father.
text_la: Filia prudens hæreditas viro suo : nam quæ confundit, in contumeliam fit genitoris.
text_el: θυγάτηρ φρονίμη κληρονομήσει ἄνδρα αὐτῆς καὶ ἡ καταισχύνουσα εἰς λύπην γεννήσαντος

text_en: She that is bold shames both her father and husband, and will not be inferior to the ungodly: and shall be disgraced by them both.
text_la: Patrem et virum confundit audax, et ab impiis non minorabitur : ab utrisque autem inhonorabitur.
text_el: πατέρα καὶ ἄνδρα καταισχύνει ἡ θρασεῖα καὶ ὑπὸ ἀμφοτέρων ἀτιμασθήσεται

text_en: A tale out of time is like music in mourning: but the stripes and instruction of wisdom are never out of time.
text_la: Musica in luctu importuna narratio : flagella et doctrina in omni tempore sapientia.
text_el: μουσικὰ ἐν πένθει ἄκαιρος διήγησις μάστιγες δὲ καὶ παιδεία ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ σοφίας

text_en: He that teaches a fool, is like one that glues a potsherd together.
text_la: Qui docet fatuum, quasi qui conglutinat testam.
text_el: συγκολλῶν ὄστρακον ὁ διδάσκων μωρόν

text_en: He that tells a word to him that hears not, is like one that wakes a man out of a deep sleep.
text_la: Qui narrat verbum non audienti, quasi qui excitat dormientem de gravi somno.
text_el: ἐξεγείρων καθεύδοντα ἐκ βαθέος ὕπνου

text_en: He speaks with one that is asleep, who utters wisdom to a fool: and in the end of the discourse he says: Who is this?
text_la: Cum dormiente loquitur qui enarrat stulto sapientiam : et in fine narrationis dicit : Quis est hic?
text_el: διηγούμενος νυστάζοντι ὁ διηγούμενος μωρῷ καὶ ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ ἐρεῖ τί ἐστιν

text_en: Weep for the dead, for his light has failed: and weep for the fool, for his understanding fails.
text_la: Supra mortuum plora, defecit enim lux ejus : et supra fatuum plora, defecit enim sensus.
text_el: ἐπὶ νεκρῷ κλαῦσον ἐξέλιπεν γὰρ φῶς καὶ ἐπὶ μωρῷ κλαῦσον ἐξέλιπεν γὰρ σύνεσιν

text_en: Weep but a little for the dead, for he is at rest.
text_la: Modicum plora super mortuum, quoniam requievit :
text_el: ἥδιον κλαῦσον ἐπὶ νεκρῷ ὅτι ἀνεπαύσατο

text_en: For the wicked life of a wicked fool is worse than death.
text_la: nequissimi enim nequissima vita super mortem fatui.
text_el: τοῦ δὲ μωροῦ ὑπὲρ θάνατον ἡ ζωὴ πονηρά

text_en: The mourning for the dead is seven days: but for a fool and an ungodly man all the days of their life.
text_la: Luctus mortui septem dies : fatui autem et impii omnes dies vitæ illorum.
text_el: πένθος νεκροῦ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι μωροῦ δὲ καὶ ἀσεβοῦς πᾶσαι αἱ ἡμέραι τῆς ζωῆς αὐτοῦ

text_en: Talk not much with a fool and go not with him that has no sense.
text_la: Cum stulto ne multum loquaris, et cum insensato ne abieris.
text_el: μετὰ ἄφρονος μὴ πληθύνῃς λόγον καὶ πρὸς ἀσύνετον μὴ πορεύου

text_en: Keep yourself from him, that you may not have trouble, and you shall not be defiled with his sin .
text_la: Serva te ab illo, ut non molestiam habeas, et non coinquinaberis peccato illius.
text_el: φύλαξαι ἀπ' αὐτοῦ ἵνα μὴ κόπον ἔχῃς καὶ οὐ μὴ μολυνθῇς ἐν τῷ ἐντιναγμῷ αὐτοῦ

text_en: Turn away from him, and you shall find rest, and shall not be wearied out with his folly.
text_la: Deflecte ab illo, et invenies requiem, et non acediaberis in stultitia illius.
text_el: ἔκκλινον ἀπ' αὐτοῦ καὶ εὑρήσεις ἀνάπαυσιν καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀκηδιάσῃς ἐν τῇ ἀπονοίᾳ αὐτοῦ

text_en: What is heavier than lead? And what other name has he but fool?
text_la: Super plumbum quid gravabitur? et quod illi aliud nomen quam fatuus?
text_el: ὑπὲρ μόλιβον τί βαρυνθήσεται καὶ τί αὐτῷ ὄνομα ἀλλ' ἢ μωρός

text_en: Sand and salt , and a mass of iron is easier to bear, than a man without sense, that is both foolish and wicked .
text_la: Arenam, et salem, et massam ferri facilius est ferre quam hominem imprudentem, et fatuum, et impium.
text_el: ἄμμον καὶ ἅλα καὶ βῶλον σιδήρου εὔκοπον ὑπενεγκεῖν ἢ ἄνθρωπον ἀσύνετον

text_en: A frame of wood bound together in the foundation of a building, shall not be loosed: so neither shall the heart that is established by advised counsel.
text_la: Loramentum ligneum colligatum in fundamento ædificii non dissolvetur, sic et cor confirmatum in cogitatione consilii.
text_el: ἱμάντωσις ξυλίνη ἐνδεδεμένη εἰς οἰκοδομὴν ἐν συσσεισμῷ οὐ διαλυθήσεται οὕτως καρδία ἐστηριγμένη ἐπὶ διανοήματος βουλῆς

text_en: The thought of him that is wise at all times, shall not be depraved by fear.
text_la: Cogitatus sensati in omni tempore metu non depravabitur.
text_el: ἐν καιρῷ οὐ δειλιάσει καρδία ἡδρασμένη ἐπὶ διανοίας συνέσεως ὡς κόσμος ψαμμωτὸς τοίχου ξυστοῦ

text_en: As pales set in high places, and plasterings made without cost, will not stand against the face of the wind:
text_la: Sicut pali in excelsis, et cæmenta sine impensa posita, contra faciem venti non permanebunt :
text_el: χάρακες ἐπὶ μετεώρου κείμενοι κατέναντι ἀνέμου οὐ μὴ ὑπομείνωσιν

text_en: So also a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool shall not resist against the violence of fear.
text_la: sic et cor timidum in cogitatione stulti contra impetum timoris non resistet.
text_el: οὕτως καρδία δειλὴ ἐπὶ διανοήματος μωροῦ κατέναντι παντὸς φόβου οὐ μὴ ὑπομείνῃ

text_en: As a fearful heart in the thought of a fool at all times will not fear, so neither shall he that continues always in the commandments of God .
text_la: Sicut cor trepidum in cogitatione fatui omni tempore non metuet, sic et qui in præceptis Dei permanet semper.

text_en: He that pricks the eye, brings out tears: and he that pricks the heart, brings forth resentment.
text_la: Pungens oculum deducit lacrimas, et qui pungit cor profert sensum.
text_el: ὁ νύσσων ὀφθαλμὸν κατάξει δάκρυα καὶ νύσσων καρδίαν ἐκφαίνει αἴσθησιν

text_en: He that flings a stone at birds, shall drive them away: so he that upbraids his friend, breaks friendship.
text_la: Mittens lapidem in volatilia, dejiciet illa : sic et qui conviciatur amico, dissolvit amicitiam.
text_el: βάλλων λίθον ἐπὶ πετεινὰ ἀποσοβεῖ αὐτά καὶ ὁ ὀνειδίζων φίλον διαλύσει φιλίαν

text_en: Although you have drawn a sword at a friend, despair not: for there may be a returning. To a friend,
text_la: Ad amicum etsi produxeris gladium, non desperes : est enim regressus. Ad amicum
text_el: ἐπὶ φίλον ἐὰν σπάσῃς ῥομφαίαν μὴ ἀφελπίσῃς ἔστιν γὰρ ἐπάνοδος

text_en: if you have opened a sad mouth, fear not, for there may be a reconciliation: except upbraiding, and reproach, and pride , and disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound: for in all these cases a friend will flee away.
text_la: si aperueris os triste, non timeas : est enim concordatio : excepto convitio, et improperio, et superbia, et mysterii revelatione, et plaga dolosa : in his omnibus effugiet amicus.
text_el: ἐπὶ φίλον ἐὰν ἀνοίξῃς στόμα μὴ εὐλαβηθῇς ἔστιν γὰρ διαλλαγή πλὴν ὀνειδισμοῦ καὶ ὑπερηφανίας καὶ μυστηρίου ἀποκαλύψεως καὶ πληγῆς δολίας ἐν τούτοις ἀποφεύξεται πᾶς φίλος

text_en: Keep fidelity with a friend in his poverty, that in his prosperity also you may rejoice.
text_la: Fidem posside cum amico in paupertate illius, ut et in bonis illius læteris.
text_el: πίστιν κτῆσαι ἐν πτωχείᾳ μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον ἵνα ἐν τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς αὐτοῦ ὁμοῦ πλησθῇς

text_en: In the time of his trouble continue faithful to him, that you may also be heir with him in his inheritance.
text_la: In tempore tribulationis illius permane illi fidelis, ut et in hæreditate illius cohæres sis.
text_el: ἐν καιρῷ θλίψεως διάμενε αὐτῷ ἵνα ἐν τῇ κληρονομίᾳ αὐτοῦ συγκληρονομήσῃς

text_en: As the vapour of a chimney, and the smoke of the fire goes up before the fire: so also injurious words, and reproaches, and threats, before blood.
text_la: Ante ignem camini vapor et fumus ignis inaltatur : sic et ante sanguinem maledicta, et contumeliæ, et minæ.
text_el: πρὸ πυρὸς ἀτμὶς καμίνου καὶ καπνός οὕτως πρὸ αἱμάτων λοιδορίαι

text_en: I will not be ashamed to salute a friend, neither will I hide myself from his face: and if any evil happen to me by him, I will bear it.
text_la: Amicum salutare non confundar, a facie illius non me abscondam : et si mala mihi evenerint per illum, sustinebo.
text_el: φίλον σκεπάσαι οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσομαι καὶ ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ κρυβῶ καὶ εἰ κακά μοι συμβήσεται δι' αὐτόν

text_en: But every one that shall hear it, will beware of him.
text_la: Omnis qui audiet cavebit se ab eo.
text_el: πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων φυλάξεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: Who will set a guard before my mouth, and a sure seal upon my lips, that I fall not by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?
text_la: Quis dabit ori meo custodiam, et super labia mea signaculum certum, ut non cadam ab ipsis, et lingua mea perdat me?
text_el: τίς δώσει ἐπὶ στόμα μου φυλακὴν καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν χειλέων μου σφραγῖδα πανοῦργον ἵνα μὴ πέσω ἀπ' αὐτῆς καὶ ἡ γλῶσσά μου ἀπολέσῃ με

text_en: O Lord , father, and sovereign ruler of my life, leave me not to their counsel: nor suffer me to fall by them.
text_la: Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in consilio eorum, nec sinas me cadere in illis.
text_el: κύριε πάτερ καὶ δέσποτα ζωῆς μου μὴ ἐγκαταλίπῃς με ἐν βουλῇ αὐτῶν μὴ ἀφῇς με πεσεῖν ἐν αὐτοῖς

text_en: Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they spare me not in their ignorances , and that their sins may not appear:
text_la: Quis superponet in cogitatu meo flagella, et in corde meo doctrinam sapientiæ, ut ignorationibus eorum non parcant mihi, et non appareant delicta eorum,
text_el: τίς ἐπιστήσει ἐπὶ τοῦ διανοήματός μου μάστιγας καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς καρδίας μου παιδείαν σοφίας ἵνα ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀγνοήμασίν μου μὴ φείσωνται καὶ οὐ μὴ παρῇ τὰ ἁμαρτήματα αὐτῶν

text_en: Lest my ignorances increase, and my offences be multiplied, and my sins abound, and I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me?
text_la: et ne adincrescant ignorantiæ meæ, et multiplicentur delicta mea, et peccata mea abundent, et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum, et gaudeat super me inimicus meus?
text_el: ὅπως μὴ πληθυνθῶσιν αἱ ἄγνοιαί μου καὶ αἱ ἁμαρτίαι μου πλεονάσωσιν καὶ πεσοῦμαι ἔναντι τῶν ὑπεναντίων καὶ ἐπιχαρεῖταί μοι ὁ ἐχθρός μου

text_en: O Lord , father, and God of my life, leave me not to their devices.
text_la: Domine, pater et Deus vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in cogitatu illorum.
text_el: κύριε πάτερ καὶ θεὲ ζωῆς μου

text_en: Give me not haughtiness of my eyes, and turn away from me all coveting .
text_la: Extollentiam oculorum meorum ne dederis mihi, et omne desiderium averte a me.
text_el: μετεωρισμὸν ὀφθαλμῶν μὴ δῷς μοι καὶ ἐπιθυμίαν ἀπόστρεψον ἀπ' ἐμοῦ

text_en: Take from me the greediness of the belly, and let not the lusts of the flesh take hold of me, and give me not over to a shameless and foolish mind.
text_la: Aufer a me ventris concupiscentias, et concubitus concupiscentiæ ne apprehendant me, et animæ irreverenti et infrunitæ ne tradas me.
text_el: κοιλίας ὄρεξις καὶ συνουσιασμὸς μὴ καταλαβέτωσάν με καὶ ψυχῇ ἀναιδεῖ μὴ παραδῷς με

text_en: Hear, O you children, the discipline of the mouth, and he that will keep it shall not perish by his lips, nor be brought to fall into most wicked works.
text_la: Doctrinam oris audite, filii : et qui custodierit illam non periet labiis, nec scandalizabitur in operibus nequissimis.
text_el: παιδείαν στόματος ἀκούσατε τέκνα καὶ ὁ φυλάσσων οὐ μὴ ἁλῷ ἐν τοῖς χείλεσιν αὐτοῦ

text_en: A sinner is caught in his own vanity, and the proud and the evil speakers shall fall thereby.
text_la: In vanitate sua apprehenditur peccator : et superbus et maledicus scandalizabitur in illis.
text_el: καταληφθήσεται ἁμαρτωλός καὶ λοίδορος καὶ ὑπερήφανος σκανδαλισθήσονται ἐν αὐτοῖς

text_en: Let not your mouth be accustomed to swearing : for in it there are many falls.
text_la: Jurationi non assuescat os tuum : multi enim casus in illa.
text_el: ὅρκῳ μὴ ἐθίσῃς τὸ στόμα σου

text_en: And let not the naming of God be usual in your mouth, and meddle not with the names of saints , for you shall not escape free from them.
text_la: Nominatio vero Dei non sit assidua in ore tuo, et nominibus sanctorum non admiscearis, quoniam non erit immunis ab eis.
text_el: καὶ ὀνομασίᾳ τοῦ ἁγίου μὴ συνεθισθῇς

text_en: For as a slave daily put to the question, is never without a blue mark: so every one that swears , and names, shall not be wholly pure from sin .
text_la: Sicut enim servus interrogatus assidue a livore non minuitur, sic omnis jurans et nominans in toto a peccato non purgabitur.
text_el: ὥσπερ γὰρ οἰκέτης ἐξεταζόμενος ἐνδελεχῶς ἀπὸ μώλωπος οὐκ ἐλαττωθήσεται οὕτως καὶ ὁ ὀμνύων καὶ ὀνομάζων διὰ παντὸς ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας οὐ μὴ καθαρισθῇ

text_en: A man that swears much, shall be filled with iniquity , and a scourge shall not depart from his house.
text_la: Vir multum jurans implebitur iniquitate, et non discedet a domo illius plaga.
text_el: ἀνὴρ πολύορκος πλησθήσεται ἀνομίας καὶ οὐκ ἀποστήσεται ἀπὸ τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ μάστιξ

text_en: And if he make it void, his sin shall be upon him, and if he dissemble it, he offends double:
text_la: Et si frustraverit, delictum illius super ipsum erit : et si dissimulaverit, delinquit dupliciter :
text_el: ἐὰν πλημμελήσῃ ἁμαρτία αὐτοῦ ἐπ' αὐτῷ κἂν ὑπερίδῃ ἥμαρτεν δισσῶς

text_en: And if he swear in vain, he shall not be justified: for his house shall be filled with his punishment.
text_la: et si in vacuum juraverit, non justificabitur : replebitur enim retributione domus illius.
text_el: καὶ εἰ διὰ κενῆς ὤμοσεν οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πλησθήσεται γὰρ ἐπαγωγῶν ὁ οἶκος αὐτοῦ

text_en: There is also another speech opposite to death, let it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob .
text_la: Est et alia loquela contraria morti : non inveniatur in hæreditate Jacob.
text_el: ἔστιν λέξις ἀντιπαραβεβλημένη θανάτῳ μὴ εὑρεθήτω ἐν κληρονομίᾳ Ιακωβ

text_en: For from the merciful all these things shall be taken away, and they shall not wallow in sins .
text_la: Etenim a misericordibus omnia hæc auferentur, et in delictis non volutabuntur.
text_el: ἀπὸ γὰρ εὐσεβῶν ταῦτα πάντα ἀποστήσεται καὶ ἐν ἁμαρτίαις οὐκ ἐγκυλισθήσονται

text_en: Let not your mouth be accustomed to indiscreet speech: for therein is the word of sin .
text_la: Indisciplinatæ loquelæ non assuescat os tuum : est enim in illa verbum peccati.
text_el: ἀπαιδευσίαν ἀσυρῆ μὴ συνεθίσῃς τὸ στόμα σου ἔστιν γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ λόγος ἁμαρτίας

text_en: Remember your father and your mother , for you sit in the midst of great men :
text_la: Memento patris et matris tuæ : in medio enim magnatorum consistis :
text_el: μνήσθητι πατρὸς καὶ μητρός σου ἀνὰ μέσον γὰρ μεγιστάνων συνεδρεύεις

text_en: Lest God forget you in their sight, and you, by your daily custom be infatuated and suffer reproach: and wish that you had not been born, and curse the day of your nativity.
text_la: ne forte obliviscatur te Deus in conspectu illorum, et assiduitate tua infatuatus, improperium patiaris, et maluisses non nasci, et diem nativitatis tuæ maledicas.
text_el: μήποτε ἐπιλάθῃ ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν καὶ τῷ ἐθισμῷ σου μωρανθῇς καὶ θελήσεις εἰ μὴ ἐγεννήθης καὶ τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ τοκετοῦ σου καταράσῃ

text_en: The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words, will never be corrected all the days of his life.
text_la: Homo assuetus in verbis improperii in omnibus diebus suis non erudietur.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος συνεθιζόμενος λόγοις ὀνειδισμοῦ ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ παιδευθῇ

text_en: Two sorts of men multiply sins , and the third brings wrath and destruction.
text_la: Duo genera abundant in peccatis, et tertium adducit iram et perditionem.
text_el: δύο εἴδη πληθύνουσιν ἁμαρτίας καὶ τὸ τρίτον ἐπάξει ὀργήν

text_en: A hot soul is a burning fire, it will never be quenched, till it devour some thing.
text_la: Anima calida quasi ignis ardens, non extinguetur donec aliquid glutiat :
text_el: ψυχὴ θερμὴ ὡς πῦρ καιόμενον οὐ μὴ σβεσθῇ ἕως ἂν καταποθῇ

text_en: And a man that is wicked in the mouth of his flesh, will not leave off till he has kindled a fire.
text_la: et homo nequam in ore carnis suæ non desinet donec incendat ignem.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος πόρνος ἐν σώματι σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ παύσηται ἕως ἂν ἐκκαύσῃ πῦρ

text_en: To a man that is a fornicator all bread is sweet, he will not be weary of sinning unto the end.
text_la: Homini fornicario omnis panis dulcis : non fatigabitur transgrediens usque ad finem.
text_el: ἀνθρώπῳ πόρνῳ πᾶς ἄρτος ἡδύς οὐ μὴ κοπάσῃ ἕως ἂν τελευτήσῃ

text_en: Every man that passes beyond his own bed, despising his own soul , and saying: Who sees me?
text_la: Omnis homo qui transgreditur lectum suum, contemnens in animam suam, et dicens : Quis me videt?
text_el: ἄνθρωπος παραβαίνων ἀπὸ τῆς κλίνης αὐτοῦ λέγων ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτοῦ τίς με ὁρᾷ

text_en: Darkness compasses me about, and the walls cover me, and no man sees me: whom do I fear? The most High will not remember my sins .
text_la: Tenebræ circumdant me, et parietes cooperiunt me, et nemo circumspicit me : quem vereor? delictorum meorum non memorabitur Altissimus.
text_el: σκότος κύκλῳ μου καὶ οἱ τοῖχοί με καλύπτουσιν καὶ οὐθείς με ὁρᾷ τί εὐλαβοῦμαι τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν μου οὐ μὴ μνησθήσεται ὁ ὕψιστος

text_en: And he understands not that his eye sees all things, for such a man's fear drives him from the fear of God , and the eyes of men fearing him:
text_la: Et non intelligit quoniam omnia videt oculus illius, quoniam expellit a se timorem Dei hujusmodi hominis timor, et oculi hominum timentes illum :
text_el: καὶ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἀνθρώπων ὁ φόβος αὐτοῦ

text_en: And he knows not that the eyes of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding round about all the ways of men , and the bottom of the deep , and looking into the hearts of men , into the most hidden parts.
text_la: et non cognovit quoniam oculi Domini multo plus lucidiores sunt super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum, et profundum abyssi, et hominum corda, intuentes in absconditas partes.
text_el: καὶ οὐκ ἔγνω ὅτι ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου μυριοπλασίως ἡλίου φωτεινότεροι ἐπιβλέποντες πάσας ὁδοὺς ἀνθρώπων καὶ κατανοοῦντες εἰς ἀπόκρυφα μέρη

text_en: For all things were known to the Lord God , before they were created : so also after they were perfected he beholds all things.
text_la: Domino enim Deo antequam crearentur omnia sunt agnita : sic et post perfectum respicit omnia.
text_el: πρὶν ἢ κτισθῆναι τὰ πάντα ἔγνωσται αὐτῷ οὕτως καὶ μετὰ τὸ συντελεσθῆναι

text_en: This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and he shall be chased as a colt: and where he suspected not, he shall be taken.
text_la: Hic in plateis civitatis vindicabitur, et quasi pullus equinus fugabitur, et ubi non speravit apprehendetur.
text_el: οὗτος ἐν πλατείαις πόλεως ἐκδικηθήσεται καὶ οὗ οὐχ ὑπενόησεν πιασθήσεται

text_en: And he shall be in disgrace with all men , because he understood not the fear of the Lord .
text_la: Et erit dedecus omnibus, eo quod non intellexerit timorem Domini.

text_en: So every woman also that leaves her husband, and brings in an heir by another:
text_la: Sic et mulier omnis relinquens virum suum, et statuens hæreditatem ex alieno matrimonio :
text_el: οὕτως καὶ γυνὴ καταλιποῦσα τὸν ἄνδρα καὶ παριστῶσα κληρονόμον ἐξ ἀλλοτρίου

text_en: For first she has been unfaithful to the law of the most High : and secondly, she has offended against her husband: thirdly, she has fornicated in adultery , and has gotten her children of another man .
text_la: primo enim in lege Altissimi incredibilis fuit : secundo in virum suum deliquit : tertio in adulterio fornicata est, et ex alio viro filios statuit sibi.
text_el: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ ἐν νόμῳ ὑψίστου ἠπείθησεν καὶ δεύτερον εἰς ἄνδρα αὐτῆς ἐπλημμέλησεν καὶ τὸ τρίτον ἐν πορνείᾳ ἐμοιχεύθη καὶ ἐξ ἀλλοτρίου ἀνδρὸς τέκνα παρέστησεν

text_en: This woman shall be brought into the assembly, and inquisition shall be made of her children.
text_la: Hæc in ecclesiam adducetur, et in filios ejus respicietur :
text_el: αὕτη εἰς ἐκκλησίαν ἐξαχθήσεται καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς ἐπισκοπὴ ἔσται

text_en: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.
text_la: non tradent filii ejus radices, et rami ejus non dabunt fructum :
text_el: οὐ διαδώσουσιν τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς εἰς ῥίζαν καὶ οἱ κλάδοι αὐτῆς οὐκ οἴσουσιν καρπόν

text_en: She shall leave her memory to be cursed , and her infamy shall not be blotted out.
text_la: derelinquet in maledictum memoriam ejus, et dedecus illius non delebitur.
text_el: καταλείψει εἰς κατάραν τὸ μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς καὶ τὸ ὄνειδος αὐτῆς οὐκ ἐξαλειφθήσεται

text_en: And they that remain shall know , that there is nothing better than the fear of God : and that there is nothing sweeter than to have regard to the commandments of the Lord .
text_la: Et agnoscent qui derelicti sunt, quoniam nihil melius est quam timor Dei, et nihil dulcius quam respicere in mandatis Domini.
text_el: καὶ ἐπιγνώσονται οἱ καταλειφθέντες ὅτι οὐθὲν κρεῖττον φόβου κυρίου καὶ οὐθὲν γλυκύτερον τοῦ προσέχειν ἐντολαῖς κυρίου

text_en: It is great glory to follow the Lord : for length of days shall be received from him.
text_la: Gloria magna est sequi Dominum : longitudo enim dierum assumetur ab eo.

text_en: Wisdom shall praise her own self, and shall be honoured in God , and shall glory in the midst of her people,
text_la: Sapientia laudabit animam suam, et in Deo honorabitur, et in medio populi sui gloriabitur,
text_el: ἡ σοφία αἰνέσει ψυχὴν αὐτῆς καὶ ἐν μέσῳ λαοῦ αὐτῆς καυχήσεται

text_en: and shall open her mouth in the churches of the most High , and shall glorify herself in the sight of his power,
text_la: et in ecclesiis Altissimi aperiet os suum, et in conspectu virtutis illius gloriabitur,
text_el: ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ὑψίστου στόμα αὐτῆς ἀνοίξει καὶ ἔναντι δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ καυχήσεται

text_en: and in the midst of her own people she shall be exalted, and shall be admired in the holy assembly .
text_la: et in medio populi sui exaltabitur, et in plenitudine sancta admirabitur,

text_en: And in the multitude of the elect she shall have praise, and among the blessed she shall be blessed , saying:
text_la: et in multitudine electorum habebit laudem, et inter benedictos benedicetur, dicens :

text_en: I came out of the mouth of the most High , the firstborn before all creatures:
text_la: Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam.
text_el: ἐγὼ ἀπὸ στόματος ὑψίστου ἐξῆλθον

text_en: I made that in the heavens there should rise light that never fails, and as a cloud I covered all the earth:
text_la: Ego feci in cælis ut oriretur lumen indeficiens, et sicut nebula texi omnem terram.
text_el: καὶ ὡς ὁμίχλη κατεκάλυψα γῆν

text_en: I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne is in a pillar of a cloud .
text_la: Ego in altissimis habitavi, et thronus meus in columna nubis.
text_el: ἐγὼ ἐν ὑψηλοῖς κατεσκήνωσα καὶ ὁ θρόνος μου ἐν στύλῳ νεφέλης

text_en: I alone have compassed the circuit of heaven , and have penetrated into the bottom of the deep , and have walked in the waves of the sea,
text_la: Gyrum cæli circuivi sola, et profundum abyssi penetravi : in fluctibus maris ambulavi.
text_el: γῦρον οὐρανοῦ ἐκύκλωσα μόνη καὶ ἐν βάθει ἀβύσσων περιεπάτησα ἐν κύμασιν θαλάσσης

text_en: and have stood in all the earth: and in every people,
text_la: Et in omni terra steti : et in omni populo,
text_el: καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ καὶ ἐν παντὶ λαῷ

text_en: and in every nation I have had the chief rule:
text_la: et in omni gente primatum habui :
text_el: καὶ ἔθνει ἐκτησάμην

text_en: And by my power I have trodden under my feet the hearts of all the high and low: and in all these I sought rest, and I shall abide in the inheritance of the Lord .
text_la: et omnium excellentium et humilium corda virtute calcavi. Et in his omnibus requiem quæsivi, et in hæreditate Domini morabor.
text_el: μετὰ τούτων πάντων ἀνάπαυσιν ἐζήτησα καὶ ἐν κληρονομίᾳ τίνος αὐλισθήσομαι

text_en: Then the creator of all things commanded, and said to me: and he that made me, rested in my tabernacle,
text_la: Tunc præcepit, et dixit mihi Creator omnium : et qui creavit me, requievit in tabernaculo meo.
text_el: τότε ἐνετείλατό μοι ὁ κτίστης ἁπάντων καὶ ὁ κτίσας με κατέπαυσεν τὴν σκηνήν μου

text_en: and he said to me: Let your dwelling be in Jacob , and your inheritance in Israel , and take root in my elect .
text_la: Et dixit mihi : In Jacob inhabita, et in Israël hæreditare, et in electis meis mitte radices.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν ἐν Ιακωβ κατασκήνωσον καὶ ἐν Ισραηλ κατακληρονομήθητι

text_en: From the beginning, and before the world, was I created , and unto the world to come I shall not cease to be, and in the holy dwelling place I have ministered before him.
text_la: Ab initio et ante sæcula creata sum, et usque ad futurum sæculum non desinam : et in habitatione sancta coram ipso ministravi.
text_el: πρὸ τοῦ αἰῶνος ἀπ' ἀρχῆς ἔκτισέν με καὶ ἕως αἰῶνος οὐ μὴ ἐκλίπω ἐν σκηνῇ ἁγίᾳ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐλειτούργησα

text_en: And so was I established in Sion, and in the holy city likewise I rested, and my power was in Jerusalem .
text_la: Et sic in Sion firmata sum, et in civitate sanctificata similiter requievi, et in Jerusalem potestas mea.
text_el: καὶ οὕτως ἐν Σιων ἐστηρίχθην ἐν πόλει ἠγαπημένῃ ὁμοίως με κατέπαυσεν καὶ ἐν Ιερουσαλημ ἡ ἐξουσία μου

text_en: And I took root in an honourable people, and in the portion of my God his inheritance, and my abode is in the full assembly of saints .
text_la: Et radicavi in populo honorificato, et in parte Dei mei hæreditas illius, et in plenitudine sanctorum detentio mea.
text_el: καὶ ἐρρίζωσα ἐν λαῷ δεδοξασμένῳ ἐν μερίδι κυρίου κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ

text_en: I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus , and as a cypress tree on mount Sion.
text_la: Quasi cedrus exaltata sum in Libano, et quasi cypressus in monte Sion :
text_el: ὡς κέδρος ἀνυψώθην ἐν τῷ Λιβάνῳ καὶ ὡς κυπάρισσος ἐν ὄρεσιν Αερμων

text_en: I was exalted like a palm tree in Cades , and as a rose plant in Jericho :
text_la: quasi palma exaltata sum in Cades, et quasi plantatio rosæ in Jericho :
text_el: ὡς φοῖνιξ ἀνυψώθην ἐν Αιγγαδοις καὶ ὡς φυτὰ ῥόδου ἐν Ιεριχω

text_en: As a fair olive tree in the plains, and as a plane tree by the water in the streets, was I exalted.
text_la: quasi oliva speciosa in campis, et quasi platanus exaltata sum juxta aquam in plateis.
text_el: ὡς ἐλαία εὐπρεπὴς ἐν πεδίῳ καὶ ἀνυψώθην ὡς πλάτανος

text_en: I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon, and aromatical balm: I yielded a sweet odour like the best myrrh:
text_la: Sicut cinnamomum et balsamum aromatizans odorem dedi; quasi myrrha electa dedi suavitatem odoris :
text_el: ὡς κιννάμωμον καὶ ἀσπάλαθος ἀρωμάτων δέδωκα ὀσμὴν καὶ ὡς σμύρνα ἐκλεκτὴ διέδωκα εὐωδίαν

text_en: And I perfumed my dwelling as storax, and galbanum, and onyx, and aloes, and as the frankincense not cut, and my odour is as the purest balm.
text_la: et quasi storax, et galbanus, et ungula, et gutta, et quasi Libanus non incisus vaporavi habitationem meam, et quasi balsamum non mistum odor meus.
text_el: ὡς χαλβάνη καὶ ὄνυξ καὶ στακτὴ καὶ ὡς λιβάνου ἀτμὶς ἐν σκηνῇ

text_en: I have stretched out my branches as the turpentine tree, and my branches are of honour and grace .
text_la: Ego quasi terebinthus extendi ramos meos, et rami mei honoris et gratiæ.
text_el: ἐγὼ ὡς τερέμινθος ἐξέτεινα κλάδους μου καὶ οἱ κλάδοι μου κλάδοι δόξης καὶ χάριτος

text_en: As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour: and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
text_la: Ego quasi vitis fructificavi suavitatem odoris : et flores mei fructus honoris et honestatis.
text_el: ἐγὼ ὡς ἄμπελος ἐβλάστησα χάριν καὶ τὰ ἄνθη μου καρπὸς δόξης καὶ πλούτου

text_en: I am the mother of fair love , and of fear, and of knowledge , and of holy hope .
text_la: Ego mater pulchræ dilectionis, et timoris, et agnitionis, et sanctæ spei.

text_en: In me is all grace of the way and of the truth , in me is all hope of life and of virtue .
text_la: In me gratia omnis viæ et veritatis : in me omnis spes vitæ et virtutis.

text_en: Come over to me, all you that desire me, and be filled with my fruits.
text_la: Transite ad me, omnes qui concupiscitis me, et a generationibus meis implemini :
text_el: προσέλθετε πρός με οἱ ἐπιθυμοῦντές μου καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν γενημάτων μου ἐμπλήσθητε

text_en: For my spirit is sweet above honey, and my inheritance above honey and the honeycomb.
text_la: spiritus enim meus super mel dulcis, et hæreditas mea super mel et favum.
text_el: τὸ γὰρ μνημόσυνόν μου ὑπὲρ τὸ μέλι γλυκύ καὶ ἡ κληρονομία μου ὑπὲρ μέλιτος κηρίον

text_en: My memory is unto everlasting generations .
text_la: Memoria mea in generatione sæculorum.

text_en: They that eat me, shall yet hunger: and they that drink me, shall yet thirst.
text_la: Qui edunt me, adhuc esurient, et qui bibunt me, adhuc sitient.
text_el: οἱ ἐσθίοντές με ἔτι πεινάσουσιν καὶ οἱ πίνοντές με ἔτι διψήσουσιν

text_en: He that hearkens to me, shall not be confounded: and they that work by me, shall not sin .
text_la: Qui audit me non confundetur, et qui operantur in me non peccabunt :
text_el: ὁ ὑπακούων μου οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι ἐν ἐμοὶ οὐχ ἁμαρτήσουσιν

text_en: They that explain me shall have life everlasting.
text_la: qui elucidant me, vitam æternam habebunt.

text_en: All these things are the book of life, and the covenant of the most High , and the knowledge of truth .
text_la: Hæc omnia liber vitæ, et testamentum Altissimi, et agnitio veritatis.
text_el: ταῦτα πάντα βίβλος διαθήκης θεοῦ ὑψίστου νόμον ὃν ἐνετείλατο ἡμῖν Μωυσῆς κληρονομίαν συναγωγαῖς Ιακωβ

text_en: Moses commanded a law in the precepts of justices, and an inheritance to the house of Jacob , and the promises to Israel .
text_la: Legem mandavit Moyses in præceptis justitiarum, et hæreditatem domui Jacob, et Israël promissiones.

text_en: He appointed to David his servant to raise up of him a most mighty king, and sitting on the throne of glory for ever.
text_la: Posuit David, puero suo, excitare regem ex ipso fortissimum, et in throno honoris sedentem in sempiternum.

text_en: Who fills up wisdom as the Phison, and as the Tigris in the days of the new fruits.
text_la: Qui implet quasi Phison sapientiam, et sicut Tigris in diebus novorum :
text_el: ὁ πιμπλῶν ὡς Φισων σοφίαν καὶ ὡς Τίγρις ἐν ἡμέραις νέων

text_en: Who makes understanding to abound as the Euphrates, who multiplies it as the Jordan in the time of harvest.
text_la: qui adimplet quasi Euphrates sensum, qui multiplicat quasi Jordanis in tempore messis :
text_el: ὁ ἀναπληρῶν ὡς Εὐφράτης σύνεσιν καὶ ὡς Ιορδάνης ἐν ἡμέραις θερισμοῦ

text_en: Who sends knowledge as the light, and rises up as Gehon in the time of the vintage.
text_la: qui mittit disciplinam sicut lucem, et assistens quasi Gehon in die vindemiæ.
text_el: ὁ ἐκφαίνων ὡς φῶς παιδείαν ὡς Γηων ἐν ἡμέραις τρυγήτου

text_en: Who first has perfect knowledge of her, and a weaker shall not search her out.
text_la: Qui perficit primus scire ipsam, et infirmior non investigabit eam.
text_el: οὐ συνετέλεσεν ὁ πρῶτος γνῶναι αὐτήν καὶ οὕτως ὁ ἔσχατος οὐκ ἐξιχνίασεν αὐτήν

text_en: For her thoughts are more vast than the sea, and her counsels more deep than the great ocean .
text_la: A mari enim abundavit cogitatio ejus, et consilium illius ab abysso magna.
text_el: ἀπὸ γὰρ θαλάσσης ἐπληθύνθη διανόημα αὐτῆς καὶ ἡ βουλὴ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ ἀβύσσου μεγάλης

text_en: I, wisdom, have poured out rivers.
text_la: Ego sapientiam effudi flumina:

text_en: I, like a brook out of a river of a mighty water; I, like a channel of a river, and like an aqueduct, came out of paradise.
text_la: ego quasi trames aquæ immensæ de fluvio : ego quasi fluvii dioryx, et sicut aquæductus exivi de paradiso.
text_el: κἀγὼ ὡς διῶρυξ ἀπὸ ποταμοῦ καὶ ὡς ὑδραγωγὸς ἐξῆλθον εἰς παράδεισον

text_en: I said: I will water my garden of plants, and I will water abundantly the fruits of my meadow.
text_la: Dixi : Rigabo hortum meum plantationum, et inebriabo prati mei fructum.
text_el: εἶπα ποτιῶ μου τὸν κῆπον καὶ μεθύσω μου τὴν πρασιάν

text_en: And behold my brook became a great river, and my river came near to a sea:
text_la: Et ecce factus est mihi trames abundans, et fluvius meus appropinquavit ad mare :
text_el: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγένετό μοι ἡ διῶρυξ εἰς ποταμόν καὶ ὁ ποταμός μου ἐγένετο εἰς θάλασσαν

text_en: For I make doctrine to shine forth to all as the morning light, and I will declare it afar off.
text_la: quoniam doctrinam quasi antelucanum illumino omnibus, et enarrabo illam usque ad longinquum.
text_el: ἔτι παιδείαν ὡς ὄρθρον φωτιῶ καὶ ἐκφανῶ αὐτὰ ἕως εἰς μακράν

text_en: I will penetrate to all the lower parts of the earth, and will behold all that sleep, and will enlighten all that hope in the Lord .
text_la: Penetrabo omnes inferiores partes terræ, et inspiciam omnes dormientes, et illuminabo omnes sperantes in Domino.

text_en: I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy , and will leave it to them that seek wisdom, and will not cease to instruct their offspring even to the holy age.
text_la: Adhuc doctrinam quasi prophetiam effundam, et relinquam illam quærentibus sapientiam, et non desinam in progenies illorum usque in ævum sanctum.
text_el: ἔτι διδασκαλίαν ὡς προφητείαν ἐκχεῶ καὶ καταλείψω αὐτὴν εἰς γενεὰς αἰώνων

text_en: See that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all that seek out the truth .
text_la: Videte quoniam non soli mihi laboravi, sed omnibus exquirentibus veritatem.
text_el: ἴδετε ὅτι οὐκ ἐμοὶ μόνῳ ἐκοπίασα ἀλλ' ἅπασιν τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσιν αὐτήν

text_en: With three things my spirit is pleased, which are approved before God and men :
text_la: In tribus placitum est spiritui meo, quæ sunt probata coram Deo et hominibus :
text_el: ἐν τρισὶν ὡραΐσθην καὶ ἀνέστην ὡραία ἔναντι κυρίου καὶ ἀνθρώπων
