text_en: The concord of brethren, and the love of neighbours, and man and wife that agree well together.
text_la: concordia fratrum, et amor proximorum, et vir et mulier bene sibi consentientes.
text_el: ὁμόνοια ἀδελφῶν καὶ φιλία τῶν πλησίον καὶ γυνὴ καὶ ἀνὴρ ἑαυτοῖς συμπεριφερόμενοι

text_en: Three sorts my soul hates , and I am greatly grieved at their life:
text_la: Tres species odivit anima mea, et aggravor valde animæ illorum :
text_el: τρία δὲ εἴδη ἐμίσησεν ἡ ψυχή μου καὶ προσώχθισα σφόδρα τῇ ζωῇ αὐτῶν

text_en: A poor man that is proud : a rich man that is a liar : an old man that is a fool, and doting.
text_la: pauperem superbum, divitem mendacem, senem fatuum et insensatum.
text_el: πτωχὸν ὑπερήφανον καὶ πλούσιον ψεύστην γέροντα μοιχὸν ἐλαττούμενον συνέσει

text_en: The things that you have not gathered in your youth, how shall you find them in your old age?
text_la: Quæ in juventute tua non congregasti, quomodo in senectute tua invenies?
text_el: ἐν νεότητι οὐ συναγείοχας καὶ πῶς ἂν εὕροις ἐν τῷ γήρᾳ σου

text_en: O how comely is judgment for a grey head, and for ancients to know counsel!
text_la: Quam speciosum canitiei judicium, et presbyteris cognoscere consilium!
text_el: ὡς ὡραῖον πολιαῖς κρίσις καὶ πρεσβυτέροις ἐπιγνῶναι βουλήν

text_en: O how comely is wisdom for the aged, and understanding and counsel to men of honour !
text_la: Quam speciosa veteranis sapientia, et gloriosus intellectus et consilium!
text_el: ὡς ὡραία γερόντων σοφία καὶ δεδοξασμένοις διανόημα καὶ βουλή

text_en: Much experience is the crown of old men , and the fear of God is their glory .
text_la: Corona senum multa peritia, et gloria illorum timor Dei.
text_el: στέφανος γερόντων πολυπειρία καὶ τὸ καύχημα αὐτῶν φόβος κυρίου

text_en: Nine things that are not to be imagined by the heart have I magnified, and the tenth I will utter to men with my tongue.
text_la: Novem insuspicabilia cordis magnificavi : et decimum dicam in lingua hominibus :
text_el: ἐννέα ὑπονοήματα ἐμακάρισα ἐν καρδίᾳ καὶ τὸ δέκατον ἐρῶ ἐπὶ γλώσσης

text_en: A man that has joy of his children: and he that lives and sees the fall of his enemies.
text_la: homo qui jucundatur in filiis, vivens et videns subversionem inimicorum suorum.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος εὐφραινόμενος ἐπὶ τέκνοις ζῶν καὶ βλέπων ἐπὶ πτώσει ἐχθρῶν

text_en: Blessed is he that dwells with a wise woman , and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not served such as are unworthy of him.
text_la: Beatus qui habitat cum muliere sensata, et qui lingua sua non est lapsus, et qui non servivit indignis se.
text_el: μακάριος ὁ συνοικῶν γυναικὶ συνετῇ καὶ ὃς ἐν γλώσσῃ οὐκ ὠλίσθησεν καὶ ὃς οὐκ ἐδούλευσεν ἀναξίῳ ἑαυτοῦ

text_en: Blessed is he that finds a true friend, and that declares justice to an ear that hears.
text_la: Beatus qui invenit amicum verum, et qui enarrat justitiam auri audienti.
text_el: μακάριος ὃς εὗρεν φρόνησιν καὶ ὁ διηγούμενος εἰς ὦτα ἀκουόντων

text_en: How great is he that finds wisdom and knowledge ! but there is none above him that fears the Lord .
text_la: Quam magnus qui invenit sapientiam et scientiam! sed non est super timentem Dominum.
text_el: ὡς μέγας ὁ εὑρὼν σοφίαν ἀλλ' οὐκ ἔστιν ὑπὲρ τὸν φοβούμενον τὸν κύριον

text_en: The fear of God has set itself above all things:
text_la: Timor Dei super omnia se superposuit.
text_el: φόβος κυρίου ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὑπερέβαλεν

text_en: Blessed is the man , to whom it is given to have the fear of God : he that holds it, to whom shall he be likened?
text_la: Beatus homo cui donatum est habere timorem Dei : qui tenet illum, cui assimilabitur?
text_el: ὁ κρατῶν αὐτοῦ τίνι ὁμοιωθήσεται

text_en: The fear of God is the beginning of his love : and the beginning of faith is to be fast joined unto it.
text_la: Timor Dei initium dilectionis ejus : fidei autem initium agglutinandum est ei.

text_en: The sadness of the heart is every plague: and the wickedness of a woman is all evil .
text_la: Omnis plaga tristitia cordis est, et omnis malitia nequitia mulieris.

text_en: And a man will choose any plague, but the plague of the heart:
text_la: Et omnem plagam, et non plagam videbit cordis :
text_el: πᾶσαν πληγὴν καὶ μὴ πληγὴν καρδίας

text_en: And any wickedness , but the wickedness of a woman :
text_la: et omnem nequitiam, et non nequitiam mulieris :
text_el: καὶ πᾶσαν πονηρίαν καὶ μὴ πονηρίαν γυναικός

text_en: And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate him:
text_la: et omnem obductum, et non obductum odientium :
text_el: πᾶσαν ἐπαγωγὴν καὶ μὴ ἐπαγωγὴν μισούντων καὶ

text_en: And any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.
text_la: et omnem vindictam, et non vindictam inimicorum.
text_el: πᾶσαν ἐκδίκησιν καὶ μὴ ἐκδίκησιν ἐχθρῶν

text_en: There is no head worse than the head of a serpent:
text_la: Non est caput nequius super caput colubri,
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν κεφαλὴ ὑπὲρ κεφαλὴν ὄφεως

text_en: And there is no anger above the anger of a woman . It will be more agreeable to abide with a lion and a dragon, than to dwell with a wicked woman .
text_la: et non est ira super iram mulieris. Commorari leoni et draconi placebit, quam habitare cum muliere nequam.
text_el: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν θυμὸς ὑπὲρ θυμὸν ἐχθροῦ συνοικῆσαι λέοντι καὶ δράκοντι εὐδοκήσω ἢ συνοικῆσαι μετὰ γυναικὸς πονηρᾶς

text_en: The wickedness of a woman changes her face: and she darkens her countenance as a bear: and shows it like sackcloth . In the midst of her neighbours,
text_la: Nequitia mulieris immutat faciem ejus : et obcæcat vultum suum tamquam ursus, et quasi saccum ostendit. In medio proximorum ejus
text_el: πονηρία γυναικὸς ἀλλοιοῖ τὴν ὅρασιν αὐτῆς καὶ σκοτοῖ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτῆς ὡς ἄρκος ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν πλησίον αὐτοῦ

text_en: her husband groaned, and hearing he sighed a little.
text_la: ingemuit vir ejus, et audiens suspiravit modicum.
text_el: ἀναπεσεῖται ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς καὶ ἀκουσίως ἀνεστέναξεν πικρά

text_en: All malice is short to the malice of a woman , let the lot of sinners fall upon her.
text_la: Brevis omnis malitia super malitiam mulieris : sors peccatorum cadat super illam.
text_el: μικρὰ πᾶσα κακία πρὸς κακίαν γυναικός κλῆρος ἁμαρτωλοῦ ἐπιπέσοι αὐτῇ

text_en: As the climbing of a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of tongue to a quiet man .
text_la: Sicut ascensus arenosus in pedibus veterani, sic mulier linguata homini quieto.
text_el: ἀνάβασις ἀμμώδης ἐν ποσὶν πρεσβυτέρου οὕτως γυνὴ γλωσσώδης ἀνδρὶ ἡσύχῳ

text_en: Look not upon a woman's beauty, and desire not a woman for beauty.
text_la: Ne respicias in mulieris speciem, et non concupiscas mulierem in specie.
text_el: μὴ προσπέσῃς ἐπὶ κάλλος γυναικὸς καὶ γυναῖκα μὴ ἐπιποθήσῃς

text_en: A woman's anger , and impudence, and confusion is great.
text_la: Mulieris ira, et irreverentia, et confusio magna.
text_el: ὀργὴ καὶ ἀναίδεια καὶ αἰσχύνη μεγάλη

text_en: A woman , if she have superiority, is contrary to her husband.
text_la: Mulier si primatum habeat, contraria est viro suo.
text_el: γυνὴ ἐὰν ἐπιχορηγῇ τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς

text_en: A wicked woman abates the courage , and makes a heavy countenance, and a wounded heart.
text_la: Cor humile, et facies tristis, et plaga cordis, mulier nequam.
text_el: καρδία ταπεινὴ καὶ πρόσωπον σκυθρωπὸν καὶ πληγὴ καρδίας γυνὴ πονηρά

text_en: Feeble hands, and disjointed knees, a woman that does not make her husband happy .
text_la: Manus debiles et genua dissoluta, mulier quæ non beatificat virum suum.
text_el: χεῖρες παρειμέναι καὶ γόνατα παραλελυμένα ἥτις οὐ μακαριεῖ τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς

text_en: From the woman came the beginning of sin , and by her we all die.
text_la: A muliere initium factum est peccati, et per illam omnes morimur.
text_el: ἀπὸ γυναικὸς ἀρχὴ ἁμαρτίας καὶ δι' αὐτὴν ἀποθνῄσκομεν πάντες

text_en: Give no issue to your water, no, not a little: nor to a wicked woman liberty to gad abroad.
text_la: Non des aquæ tuæ exitum, nec modicum : nec mulieri nequam veniam prodeundi.
text_el: μὴ δῷς ὕδατι διέξοδον μηδὲ γυναικὶ πονηρᾷ παρρησίαν

text_en: If she walk not at your hand, she will confound you in the sight of your enemies.
text_la: Si non ambulaverit ad manum tuam, confundet te in conspectu inimicorum.
text_el: εἰ μὴ πορεύεται κατὰ χεῖράς σου

text_en: Cut her off from your flesh, lest she always abuse you.
text_la: A carnibus tuis abscinde illam, ne semper te abutatur.
text_el: ἀπὸ τῶν σαρκῶν σου ἀπότεμε αὐτήν

text_en: Happy is the husband of a good wife: for the number of his years is double.
text_la: Mulieris bonæ beatus vir : numerus enim annorum illius duplex.
text_el: γυναικὸς ἀγαθῆς μακάριος ὁ ἀνήρ καὶ ἀριθμὸς τῶν ἡμερῶν αὐτοῦ διπλάσιος

text_en: A virtuous woman rejoices her husband, and shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.
text_la: Mulier fortis oblectat virum suum, et annos vitæ illius in pace implebit.
text_el: γυνὴ ἀνδρεία εὐφραίνει τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς καὶ τὰ ἔτη αὐτοῦ πληρώσει ἐν εἰρήνῃ

text_en: A good wife is a good portion, she shall be given in the portion of them that fear God , to a man for his good deeds.
text_la: Pars bona mulier bona, in parte timentium Deum dabitur viro pro factis bonis :
text_el: γυνὴ ἀγαθὴ μερὶς ἀγαθή ἐν μερίδι φοβουμένων κύριον δοθήσεται

text_en: Rich or poor, if his heart is good , his countenance shall be cheerful at all times.
text_la: divitis autem et pauperis cor bonum, in omni tempore vultus illorum hilaris.
text_el: πλουσίου δὲ καὶ πτωχοῦ καρδία ἀγαθή ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ πρόσωπον ἱλαρόν

text_en: Of three things my heart has been afraid, and at the fourth my face has trembled:
text_la: A tribus timuit cor meum, et in quarto facies mea metuit :
text_el: ἀπὸ τριῶν εὐλαβήθη ἡ καρδία μου καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ τετάρτῳ προσώπῳ ἐδεήθην

text_en: The accusation of a city, and the gathering together of the people:
text_la: delaturam civitatis, et collectionem populi :
text_el: διαβολὴν πόλεως καὶ ἐκκλησίαν ὄχλου

text_en: And a false calumny , all are more grievous than death.
text_la: calumniam mendacem super mortem omnia gravia:
text_el: καὶ καταψευσμόν ὑπὲρ θάνατον πάντα μοχθηρά

text_en: A jealous woman is the grief and mourning of the heart.
text_la: dolor cordis et luctus, mulier zelotypa.
text_el: ἄλγος καρδίας καὶ πένθος γυνὴ

text_en: With a jealous woman is a scourge of the tongue which communicates with all.
text_la: In muliere zelotypa flagellum linguæ, omnibus communicans.
text_el: ἀντίζηλος ἐπὶ γυναικὶ καὶ μάστιξ γλώσσης πᾶσιν ἐπικοινωνοῦσα

text_en: As a yoke of oxen that is moved to and fro, so also is a wicked woman : he that has hold of her, is as he that takes hold of a scorpion.
text_la: Sicut boum jugum quod movetur, ita et mulier nequam : qui tenet illam quasi qui apprehendit scorpionem.
text_el: βοοζύγιον σαλευόμενον γυνὴ πονηρά ὁ κρατῶν αὐτῆς ὡς ὁ δρασσόμενος σκορπίου

text_en: A drunken woman is a great wrath : and her reproach and shame shall not be hid.
text_la: Mulier ebriosa ira magna, et contumelia : et turpitudo illius non tegetur.
text_el: ὀργὴ μεγάλη γυνὴ μέθυσος καὶ ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτῆς οὐ συγκαλύψει

text_en: The fornication of a woman shall be known by the haughtiness of her eyes and by her eyelids.
text_la: Fornicatio mulieris in extollentia oculorum, et in palpebris illius agnoscetur.
text_el: πορνεία γυναικὸς ἐν μετεωρισμοῖς ὀφθαλμῶν καὶ ἐν τοῖς βλεφάροις αὐτῆς γνωσθήσεται

text_en: On a daughter that turns not away herself, set a strict watch: lest finding an opportunity she abuse herself.
text_la: In filia non avertente se, firma custodiam, ne inventa occasione utatur se.
text_el: ἐπὶ θυγατρὶ ἀδιατρέπτῳ στερέωσον φυλακήν ἵνα μὴ εὑροῦσα ἄνεσιν ἑαυτῇ χρήσηται

text_en: Take heed of the impudence of her eyes, and wonder not if she slight you.
text_la: Ab omni irreverentia oculorum ejus cave, et ne mireris si te neglexerit.
text_el: ὀπίσω ἀναιδοῦς ὀφθαλμοῦ φύλαξαι καὶ μὴ θαυμάσῃς ἐὰν εἰς σὲ πλημμελήσῃ

text_en: She will open her mouth as a thirsty traveller to the fountain, and will drink of every water near her, and will sit down by every hedge, and open her quiver against every arrow, until she fail.
text_la: Sicut viator sitiens ad fontem os aperiet, et ab omni aqua proxima bibet, et contra omnem palum sedebit, et contra omnem sagittam aperiet pharetram donec deficiat.
text_el: ὡς διψῶν ὁδοιπόρος τὸ στόμα ἀνοίξει καὶ ἀπὸ παντὸς ὕδατος τοῦ σύνεγγυς πίεται κατέναντι παντὸς πασσάλου καθήσεται καὶ ἔναντι βέλους ἀνοίξει φαρέτραν

text_en: The grace of a diligent woman shall delight her husband, and shall fat his bones.
text_la: Gratia mulieris sedulæ delectabit virum suum, et ossa illius impinguabit.
text_el: χάρις γυναικὸς τέρψει τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς καὶ τὰ ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ πιανεῖ

text_en: Her discipline is the gift of God .
text_la: Disciplina illius datum Dei est.
text_el: ἡ ἐπιστήμη αὐτῆς δόσις κυρίου

text_en: Such is a wise and silent woman , and there is nothing so much worth as a well instructed soul .
text_la: Mulier sensata et tacita, non est immutatio eruditæ animæ.
text_el: γυνὴ σιγηρά καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἀντάλλαγμα πεπαιδευμένης ψυχῆς

text_en: A holy and shamefaced woman is grace upon grace .
text_la: Gratia super gratiam mulier sancta et pudorata.
text_el: χάρις ἐπὶ χάριτι γυνὴ αἰσχυντηρά

text_en: And no price is worthy of a continent soul .
text_la: Omnis autem ponderatio non est digna continentis animæ.
text_el: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν σταθμὸς πᾶς ἄξιος ἐγκρατοῦς ψυχῆς

text_en: As the sun when it rises to the world in the high places of God , so is the beauty of a good wife for the ornament of her house.
text_la: Sicut sol oriens mundo in altissimis Dei, sic mulieris bonæ species in ornamentum domus ejus.
text_el: ἥλιος ἀνατέλλων ἐν ὑψίστοις κυρίου καὶ κάλλος ἀγαθῆς γυναικὸς ἐν κόσμῳ οἰκίας αὐτῆς

text_en: As the lamp shining upon the holy candlestick , so is the beauty of the face in a ripe age,
text_la: Lucerna splendens super candelabrum sanctum, et species faciei super ætatem stabilem.
text_el: λύχνος ἐκλάμπων ἐπὶ λυχνίας ἁγίας καὶ κάλλος προσώπου ἐπὶ ἡλικίᾳ στασίμῃ

text_en: as golden pillars upon bases of silver, so are the firm feet upon the soles of a steady woman .
text_la: Columnæ aureæ super bases argenteas, et pedes firmi super plantas stabilis mulieris.
text_el: στῦλοι χρύσεοι ἐπὶ βάσεως ἀργυρᾶς καὶ πόδες ὡραῖοι ἐπὶ στέρνοις εὐσταθοῦς

text_en: As everlasting foundations upon a solid rock, so the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman .
text_la: Fundamenta æterna supra petram solidam, et mandata Dei in corde mulieris sanctæ.

text_en: At two things my heart is grieved, and the third brings anger upon me.
text_la: In duobus contristatum est cor meum, et in tertio iracundia mihi advenit :
text_el: ἐπὶ δυσὶ λελύπηται ἡ καρδία μου καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ τρίτῳ θυμός μοι ἐπῆλθεν

text_en: A man of war fainting through poverty, and a man of sense despised :
text_la: vir bellator deficiens per inopiam; et vir sensatus contemptus;
text_el: ἀνὴρ πολεμιστὴς ὑστερῶν δι' ἔνδειαν καὶ ἄνδρες συνετοὶ ἐὰν σκυβαλισθῶσιν

text_en: And he that passes over from justice to sin , God has prepared such an one for the sword.
text_la: et qui transgreditur a justitia ad peccatum : Deus paravit eum ad rhomphæam.
text_el: ἐπανάγων ἀπὸ δικαιοσύνης ἐπὶ ἁμαρτίαν ὁ κύριος ἑτοιμάσει εἰς ῥομφαίαν αὐτόν

text_en: Two sorts of callings have appeared to me hard and dangerous: a merchant is hardly free from negligence: and a huckster shall not be justified from the sins of the lips.
text_la: Duæ species difficiles et periculosæ mihi apparuerunt : difficile exuitur negotians a negligentia, et non justificabitur caupo a peccatis labiorum.
text_el: μόλις ἐξελεῖται ἔμπορος ἀπὸ πλημμελείας καὶ οὐ δικαιωθήσεται κάπηλος ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας

text_en: Through poverty many have sinned : and he that seeks to be enriched, turns away his eye.
text_la: Propter inopiam multi deliquerunt : et qui quærit locupletari avertit oculum suum.
text_el: χάριν διαφόρου πολλοὶ ἥμαρτον καὶ ὁ ζητῶν πληθῦναι ἀποστρέψει ὀφθαλμόν

text_en: As a stake sticks fast in the midst of the joining of stones, so also in the midst of selling and buying, sin shall stick fast.
text_la: Sicut in medio compaginis lapidum palus figitur, sic et inter medium venditionis et emptionis angustiabitur peccatum :
text_el: ἀνὰ μέσον ἁρμῶν λίθων παγήσεται πάσσαλος καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον πράσεως καὶ ἀγορασμοῦ συντριβήσεται ἁμαρτία

text_en: Sin shall be destroyed with the sinner.
text_la: conteretur cum delinquente delictum.

text_en: Unless you hold yourself diligently in the fear of the Lord , your house shall quickly be overthrown.
text_la: Si non in timore Domini tenueris te instanter, cito subvertetur domus tua.
text_el: ἐὰν μὴ ἐν φόβῳ κυρίου κρατήσῃ κατὰ σπουδήν ἐν τάχει καταστραφήσεται αὐτοῦ ὁ οἶκος

text_en: As when one sifts with a sieve, the dust will remain: so will the perplexity of a man in his thoughts.
text_la: Sicut in percussura cribri remanebit pulvis, sic aporia hominis in cogitatu illius.
text_el: ἐν σείσματι κοσκίνου διαμένει κοπρία οὕτως σκύβαλα ἀνθρώπου ἐν λογισμῷ αὐτοῦ

text_en: The furnace tries the potter's vessels, and the trial of affliction just men .
text_la: Vasa figuli probat fornax, et homines justos tentatio tribulationis.
text_el: σκεύη κεραμέως δοκιμάζει κάμινος καὶ πειρασμὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐν διαλογισμῷ αὐτοῦ

text_en: As the dressing of a tree shows the fruit thereof, so a word out of the thought of the heart of man .
text_la: Sicut rusticatio de ligno ostendit fructum illius, sic verbum ex cogitatu cordis hominis.
text_el: γεώργιον ξύλου ἐκφαίνει ὁ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ οὕτως λόγος ἐνθυμήματος καρδίας ἀνθρώπου

text_en: Praise not a man before he speaks, for this is the trial of men .
text_la: Ante sermonem non laudes virum : hæc enim tentatio est hominum.
text_el: πρὸ λογισμοῦ μὴ ἐπαινέσῃς ἄνδρα οὗτος γὰρ πειρασμὸς ἀνθρώπων

text_en: If you follow justice , you shall obtain her: and shall put her on as a long robe of honour , and you shall dwell with her: and she shall protect you for ever, and in the day of acknowledgment you shall find a strong foundation.
text_la: Si sequaris justitiam, apprehendes illam, et indues quasi poderem honoris : et inhabitabis cum ea, et proteget te in sempiternum, et in die agnitionis invenies firmamentum.
text_el: ἐὰν διώκῃς τὸ δίκαιον καταλήμψῃ καὶ ἐνδύσῃ αὐτὸ ὡς ποδήρη δόξης

text_en: Birds resort unto their like: so truth will return to them that practise her.
text_la: Volatilia ad sibi similia conveniunt : et veritas ad eos qui operantur illam revertetur.
text_el: πετεινὰ πρὸς τὰ ὅμοια αὐτοῖς καταλύσει καὶ ἀλήθεια πρὸς τοὺς ἐργαζομένους αὐτὴν ἐπανήξει

text_en: The lion always lies in wait for prey: so do sins for them that work iniquities .
text_la: Leo venationi insidiatur semper : sic peccata operantibus iniquitates.
text_el: λέων θήραν ἐνεδρεύει οὕτως ἁμαρτία ἐργαζομένους ἄδικα

text_en: A holy man continues in wisdom as the sun: but a fool is changed as the moon.
text_la: Homo sanctus in sapientia manet sicut sol : nam stultus sicut luna mutatur.
text_el: διήγησις εὐσεβοῦς διὰ παντὸς σοφία ὁ δὲ ἄφρων ὡς σελήνη ἀλλοιοῦται

text_en: In the midst of the unwise keep in the word till its time: but be continually among men that think.
text_la: In medio insensatorum serva verbum tempori : in medio autem cogitantium assiduus esto.
text_el: εἰς μέσον ἀσυνέτων συντήρησον καιρόν εἰς μέσον δὲ διανοουμένων ἐνδελέχιζε

text_en: The discourse of sinners is hateful , and their laughter is at the pleasures of sin .
text_la: Narratio peccantium odiosa, et risus illorum in deliciis peccati.
text_el: διήγησις μωρῶν προσόχθισμα καὶ ὁ γέλως αὐτῶν ἐν σπατάλῃ ἁμαρτίας

text_en: The speech that swears much shall make the hair of the head stand upright: and its irreverence shall make one stop his ears.
text_la: Loquela multum jurans horripilationem capiti statuet, et irreverentia ipsius obturatio aurium.
text_el: λαλιὰ πολυόρκου ἀνορθώσει τρίχας καὶ ἡ μάχη αὐτῶν ἐμφραγμὸς ὠτίων

text_en: In the quarrels of the road is the shedding of blood: and their cursing is a grievous hearing.
text_la: Effusio sanguinis in rixa superborum, et maledictio illorum auditus gravis.
text_el: ἔκχυσις αἵματος μάχη ὑπερηφάνων καὶ ἡ διαλοιδόρησις αὐτῶν ἀκοὴ μοχθηρά

text_en: He that discloses the secret of a friend loses his credit, and shall never find a friend to his mind.
text_la: Qui denudat arcana amici fidem perdit, et non inveniet amicum ad animum suum.
text_el: ὁ ἀποκαλύπτων μυστήρια ἀπώλεσεν πίστιν καὶ οὐ μὴ εὕρῃ φίλον πρὸς τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: Love your neighbour, and be joined to him with fidelity.
text_la: Dilige proximum, et conjungere fide cum illo.
text_el: στέρξον φίλον καὶ πιστώθητι μετ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: But if you discover his secrets, follow no more after him.
text_la: Quod si denudaveris absconsa illius, non persequeris post eum.
text_el: ἐὰν δὲ ἀποκαλύψῃς τὰ μυστήρια αὐτοῦ μὴ καταδιώξῃς ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ

text_en: For as a man that destroys his friend, so is he that destroys the friendship of his neighbour.
text_la: Sicut enim homo qui perdit amicum suum, sic et qui perdit amicitiam proximi sui.
text_el: καθὼς γὰρ ἀπώλεσεν ἄνθρωπος τὸν νεκρὸν αὐτοῦ οὕτως ἀπώλεσας τὴν φιλίαν τοῦ πλησίον

text_en: And as one that lets a bird go out of his hand, so have you let your neighbour go, and you shall not get him again.
text_la: Et sicut qui dimittit avem de manu sua, sic dereliquisti proximum tuum, et non eum capies.
text_el: καὶ ὡς πετεινὸν ἐκ χειρός σου ἀπέλυσας οὕτως ἀφῆκας τὸν πλησίον καὶ οὐ θηρεύσεις αὐτόν

text_en: Follow after him no more, for he has gone afar off, he is fled, as a roe escaped out of the snare because his soul is wounded.
text_la: Non illum sequaris, quoniam longe abest : effugit enim quasi caprea de laqueo, quoniam vulnerata est anima ejus :
text_el: μὴ αὐτὸν διώξῃς ὅτι μακρὰν ἀπέστη καὶ ἐξέφυγεν ὡς δορκὰς ἐκ παγίδος ὅτι τραῦμα ἔστιν

text_en: You can no more bind him up. And of a curse there is reconciliation:
text_la: ultra eum non poteris colligare. Et maledicti est concordatio :
text_el: καταδῆσαι καὶ λοιδορίας ἔστιν διαλλαγή

text_en: But to disclose the secrets of a friend, leaves no hope to an unhappy soul .
text_la: denudare autem amici mysteria, desperatio est animæ infelicis.
text_el: ὁ δὲ ἀποκαλύψας μυστήρια ἀφήλπισεν

text_en: He that winks with the eye forges wicked things, and no man will cast him off:
text_la: Annuens oculo fabricat iniqua, et nemo eum abjiciet.
text_el: διανεύων ὀφθαλμῷ τεκταίνει κακά καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτὰ ἀποστήσει ἀπ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: In the sight of your eyes he will sweeten his mouth, and will admire your words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and on your words he will lay a stumbling block.
text_la: In conspectu oculorum tuorum condulcabit os suum, et super sermones tuos admirabitur : novissime autem pervertet os suum, et in verbis tuis dabit scandalum.
text_el: ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου γλυκανεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν λόγων σου ἐκθαυμάσει ὕστερον δὲ διαστρέψει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου δώσει σκάνδαλον

text_en: I have hated many things but not like him, and the Lord will hate him.
text_la: Multa odivi, et non coæquavi ei, et Dominus odiet illum.
text_el: πολλὰ ἐμίσησα καὶ οὐχ ὡμοίωσα αὐτῷ καὶ ὁ κύριος μισήσει αὐτόν

text_en: If one cast a stone on high, it will fall upon his own head: and the deceitful stroke will wound the deceitful.
text_la: Qui in altum mittit lapidem, super caput ejus cadet : et plaga dolosa dolosi dividet vulnera.
text_el: ὁ βάλλων λίθον εἰς ὕψος ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ βάλλει καὶ πληγὴ δολία διελεῖ τραύματα

text_en: He that digs a pit, shall fall into it: and he that sets a stone for his neighbour, shall stumble upon it: and he that lays a snare for another, shall perish in it.
text_la: Et qui foveam fodit incidet in eam : et qui statuit lapidem proximo offendet in eo : et qui laqueum alii ponit, peribit in illo.
text_el: ὁ ὀρύσσων βόθρον εἰς αὐτὸν ἐμπεσεῖται καὶ ὁ ἱστῶν παγίδα ἐν αὐτῇ ἁλώσεται

text_en: A mischievous counsel shall be rolled back upon the author, and he shall not know from whence it comes to him.
text_la: Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur, et non agnoscet unde adveniat illi.
text_el: ὁ ποιῶν πονηρά εἰς αὐτὸν κυλισθήσεται καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐπιγνῷ πόθεν ἥκει αὐτῷ

text_en: Mockery and reproach are of the proud , and vengeance as a lion shall lie in wait for him.
text_la: Illusio et improperium superborum, et vindicta sicut leo insidiabitur illi.
text_el: ἐμπαιγμὸς καὶ ὀνειδισμὸς ὑπερηφάνῳ καὶ ἡ ἐκδίκησις ὡς λέων ἐνεδρεύσει αὐτόν

text_en: They shall perish in a snare that are delighted with the fall of the just : and sorrow shall consume them before they die.
text_la: Laqueo peribunt qui oblectantur casu justorum, dolor autem consumet illos antequam moriantur.
text_el: παγίδι ἁλώσονται οἱ εὐφραινόμενοι πτώσει εὐσεβῶν καὶ ὀδύνη καταναλώσει αὐτοὺς πρὸ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτῶν

text_en: Anger and fury are both of them abominable, and the sinful man shall be subject to them.
text_la: Ira et furor utraque execrabilia sunt, et vir peccator continens erit illorum.
text_el: μῆνις καὶ ὀργή καὶ ταῦτά ἐστιν βδελύγματα καὶ ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλὸς ἐγκρατὴς ἔσται αὐτῶν

text_en: He that seeks to revenge himself, shall find vengeance from the Lord , and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.
text_la: Qui vindicari vult, a Domino inveniet vindictam, et peccata illius servans servabit.
text_el: ὁ ἐκδικῶν παρὰ κυρίου εὑρήσει ἐκδίκησιν καὶ τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ διατηρῶν διατηρήσει

text_en: Forgive your neighbour if he has hurt you: and then shall your sins be forgiven to you when you pray .
text_la: Relinque proximo tuo nocenti te, et tunc deprecanti tibi peccata solventur.
text_el: ἄφες ἀδίκημα τῷ πλησίον σου καὶ τότε δεηθέντος σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου λυθήσονται

text_en: Man to man reserves anger , and does he seek remedy of God ?
text_la: Homo homini reservat iram, et a Deo quærit medelam :
text_el: ἄνθρωπος ἀνθρώπῳ συντηρεῖ ὀργήν καὶ παρὰ κυρίου ζητεῖ ἴασιν

text_en: He has no mercy on a man like himself, and does he entreat for his own sins ?
text_la: in hominem similem sibi non habet misericordiam, et de peccatis suis deprecatur.
text_el: ἐπ' ἄνθρωπον ὅμοιον αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔχει ἔλεος καὶ περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτοῦ δεῖται

text_en: He that is but flesh, nourishes anger , and does he ask forgiveness of God ? Who shall obtain pardon for his sins ?
text_la: Ipse cum caro sit reservat iram, et propitiationem petit a Deo : quis exorabit pro delictis illius?
text_el: αὐτὸς σὰρξ ὢν διατηρεῖ μῆνιν τίς ἐξιλάσεται τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ

text_en: Remember your last things, and let enmity cease:
text_la: Memento novissimorum, et desine inimicari :
text_el: μνήσθητι τὰ ἔσχατα καὶ παῦσαι ἐχθραίνων

text_en: For corruption and death hang over in his commandments.
text_la: tabitudo enim et mors imminent in mandatis ejus.
text_el: καταφθορὰν καὶ θάνατον καὶ ἔμμενε ἐντολαῖς

text_en: Remember the fear of God , and be not angry with your neighbour.
text_la: Memorare timorem Dei, et non irascaris proximo.
text_el: μνήσθητι ἐντολῶν καὶ μὴ μηνίσῃς τῷ πλησίον

text_en: Remember the covenant of the most High , and overlook the ignorance of your neighbour.
text_la: Memorare testamentum Altissimi, et despice ignorantiam proximi.
text_el: καὶ διαθήκην ὑψίστου καὶ πάριδε ἄγνοιαν

text_en: Refrain from strife, and you shall diminish your sins .
text_la: Abstine te a lite, et minues peccata.
text_el: ἀπόσχου ἀπὸ μάχης καὶ ἐλαττώσεις ἁμαρτίας

text_en: For a passionate man kindles strife, and a sinful man will trouble his friends, and bring in debate in the midst of them that are at peace.
text_la: Homo enim iracundus incendit litem, et vir peccator turbabit amicos, et in medio pacem habentium immittet inimicitiam.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος γὰρ θυμώδης ἐκκαύσει μάχην καὶ ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλὸς ταράξει φίλους καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον εἰρηνευόντων ἐμβαλεῖ διαβολήν

text_en: For as the wood of the forest is, so the fire burns, and as a man's strength is, so shall his anger be, and according to his riches he shall increase his anger .
text_la: Secundum enim ligna silvæ sic ignis exardescit : et secundum virtutem hominis sic iracundia illius erit, et secundum substantiam suam exaltabit iram suam.
text_el: κατὰ τὴν ὕλην τοῦ πυρὸς οὕτως ἐκκαυθήσεται καὶ κατὰ τὴν στερέωσιν τῆς μάχης ἐκκαυθήσεται κατὰ τὴν ἰσχὺν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁ θυμὸς αὐτοῦ ἔσται καὶ κατὰ τὸν πλοῦτον ἀνυψώσει ὀργὴν αὐτοῦ

text_en: A hasty contention kindles a fire and a hasty quarrel sheds blood and a tongue that bears witness brings death.
text_la: Certamen festinatum incendit ignem, et lis festinans effundit sanguinem : et lingua testificans adducit mortem.
text_el: ἔρις κατασπευδομένη ἐκκαίει πῦρ καὶ μάχη κατασπεύδουσα ἐκχέει αἷμα

text_en: If you blow the spark, it shall burn as a fire: and if you spit upon it, it shall be quenched: both come out of the mouth.
text_la: Si sufflaveris in scintillam, quasi ignis exardebit : et si exspueris super illam, extinguetur : utraque ex ore proficiscuntur.
text_el: ἐὰν φυσήσῃς εἰς σπινθῆρα ἐκκαήσεται καὶ ἐὰν πτύσῃς ἐπ' αὐτόν σβεσθήσεται καὶ ἀμφότερα ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου ἐκπορεύεται

text_en: The whisperer and the double tongue is accursed : for he has troubled many that were at peace.
text_la: Susurro et bilinguis maledictus, multos enim turbabit pacem habentes.
text_el: ψίθυρον καὶ δίγλωσσον καταράσασθε πολλοὺς γὰρ εἰρηνεύοντας ἀπώλεσεν

text_en: The tongue of a third person has disquieted many, and scattered them from nation to nation.
text_la: Lingua tertia multos commovit, et dispersit illos de gente in gentem.
text_el: γλῶσσα τρίτη πολλοὺς ἐσάλευσεν καὶ διέστησεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ ἔθνους εἰς ἔθνος

text_en: It has destroyed the strong cities of the rich , and has overthrown the houses of great men .
text_la: Civitates muratas divitum destruxit, et domus magnatorum effodit.
text_el: καὶ πόλεις ὀχυρὰς καθεῖλεν καὶ οἰκίας μεγιστάνων κατέστρεψεν

text_en: It has cut in pieces the forces of people, and undone strong nations.
text_la: Virtutes populorum concidit, et gentes fortes dissolvit.

text_en: The tongue of a third person has cast out valiant women , and deprived them of their labours.
text_la: Lingua tertia mulieres viratas ejecit, et privavit illas laboribus suis.
text_el: γλῶσσα τρίτη γυναῖκας ἀνδρείας ἐξέβαλεν καὶ ἐστέρεσεν αὐτὰς τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν

text_en: He that hearkens to it, shall never have rest, neither shall he have a friend in whom he may repose.
text_la: Qui respicit illam non habebit requiem, nec habebit amicum in quo requiescat.
text_el: ὁ προσέχων αὐτῇ οὐ μὴ εὕρῃ ἀνάπαυσιν οὐδὲ κατασκηνώσει μεθ' ἡσυχίας

text_en: The stroke of a whip makes a blue mark: but the stroke of the tongue will break the bones.
text_la: Flagelli plaga livorem facit : plaga autem linguæ comminuet ossa.
text_el: πληγὴ μάστιγος ποιεῖ μώλωπα πληγὴ δὲ γλώσσης συγκλάσει ὀστᾶ

text_en: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have perished by their own tongue.
text_la: Multi ceciderunt in ore gladii : sed non sic quasi qui interierunt per linguam suam.
text_el: πολλοὶ ἔπεσαν ἐν στόματι μαχαίρας καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ πεπτωκότες διὰ γλῶσσαν

text_en: Blessed is he that is defended from a wicked tongue, that has not passed into the wrath thereof, and that has not drawn the yoke thereof, and has not been bound in its bands.
text_la: Beatus qui tectus est a lingua nequam, qui in iracundiam illius non transivit, et qui non attraxit jugum illius, et in vinculis ejus non est ligatus :
text_el: μακάριος ὁ σκεπασθεὶς ἀπ' αὐτῆς ὃς οὐ διῆλθεν ἐν τῷ θυμῷ αὐτῆς ὃς οὐχ εἵλκυσεν τὸν ζυγὸν αὐτῆς καὶ ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς αὐτῆς οὐκ ἐδέθη

text_en: For its yoke is a yoke of iron: and its bands are bands of brass.
text_la: jugum enim illius jugum ferreum est, et vinculum illius vinculum æreum est;
text_el: ὁ γὰρ ζυγὸς αὐτῆς ζυγὸς σιδηροῦς καὶ οἱ δεσμοὶ αὐτῆς δεσμοὶ χάλκειοι

text_en: The death thereof is a most evil death: and hell is preferable to it.
text_la: mors illius mors nequissima : et utilis potius infernus quam illa.
text_el: θάνατος πονηρὸς ὁ θάνατος αὐτῆς καὶ λυσιτελὴς μᾶλλον ὁ ᾅδης αὐτῆς

text_en: Its continuance shall not be for a long time, but it shall possess the ways of the unjust : and the just shall not be burnt with its flame.
text_la: Perseverantia illius non permanebit, sed obtinebit vias injustorum, et in flamma sua non comburet justos.
text_el: οὐ μὴ κρατήσῃ εὐσεβῶν καὶ ἐν τῇ φλογὶ αὐτῆς οὐ καήσονται

text_en: They that forsake God shall fall into it, and it shall burn in them, and shall not be quenched, and it shall be sent upon them as a lion, and as a leopard it shall tear them.
text_la: Qui relinquunt Deum incident in illam, et exardebit in illis, et non extinguetur, et immittetur in illos quasi leo, et quasi pardus lædet illos.
text_el: οἱ καταλείποντες κύριον ἐμπεσοῦνται εἰς αὐτήν καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐκκαήσεται καὶ οὐ μὴ σβεσθῇ ἐπαποσταλήσεται αὐτοῖς ὡς λέων καὶ ὡς πάρδαλις λυμανεῖται αὐτούς

text_en: Hedge in your ears with thorns, hear not a wicked tongue, and make doors and bars to your mouth.
text_la: Sepi aures tuas spinis : linguam nequam noli audire : et ori tuo facito ostia et seras.
text_el: ἰδὲ περίφραξον τὸ κτῆμά σου ἀκάνθαις

text_en: Melt down your gold and silver, and make a balance for your words, and a just bridle for your mouth:
text_la: Aurum tuum et argentum tuum confla, et verbis tuis facito stateram, et frenos ori tuo rectos :
text_el: τὸ ἀργύριόν σου καὶ τὸ χρυσίον κατάδησον καὶ τοῖς λόγοις σου ποίησον ζυγὸν καὶ σταθμὸν καὶ τῷ στόματί σου ποίησον θύραν καὶ μοχλόν

text_en: And take heed lest you slip with your tongue, and fall in the sight of your enemies who lie in wait for you, and your fall be incurable unto death.
text_la: et attende ne forte labaris in lingua, et cadas in conspectu inimicorum insidiantium tibi, et sit casus tuus insanabilis in mortem.
text_el: πρόσεχε μήπως ὀλίσθῃς ἐν αὐτῇ μὴ πέσῃς κατέναντι ἐνεδρεύοντος

text_en: He that shows mercy, lends to his neighbour: and he that is stronger in hand, keeps the commandments.
text_la: Qui facit misericordiam fœneratur proximo suo : et qui prævalet manu mandata servat.
text_el: ὁ ποιῶν ἔλεος δανιεῖ τῷ πλησίον καὶ ὁ ἐπισχύων τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ τηρεῖ ἐντολάς

text_en: Lend to your neighbour in the time of his need, and pay your neighbour again in due time.
text_la: Fœnerare proximo tuo in tempore necessitatis illius : et iterum redde proximo in tempore suo.
text_el: δάνεισον τῷ πλησίον ἐν καιρῷ χρείας αὐτοῦ καὶ πάλιν ἀπόδος τῷ πλησίον εἰς τὸν καιρόν

text_en: Keep your word, and deal faithfully with him: and you shall always find that which is necessary for you.
text_la: Confirma verbum, et fideliter age cum illo : et in omni tempore invenies quod tibi necessarium est.
text_el: στερέωσον λόγον καὶ πιστώθητι μετ' αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ εὑρήσεις τὴν χρείαν σου

text_en: Many have looked upon a thing lent as a thing found, and have given trouble to them that helped them.
text_la: Multi quasi inventionem æstimaverunt fœnus, et præstiterunt molestiam his qui se adjuverunt.
text_el: πολλοὶ ὡς εὕρεμα ἐνόμισαν δάνος καὶ παρέσχον κόπον τοῖς βοηθήσασιν αὐτοῖς

text_en: Till they receive, they kiss the hands of the lender, and in promises they humble their voice:
text_la: Donec accipiant, osculantur manus dantis, et in promissionibus humiliant vocem suam :
text_el: ἕως οὗ λάβῃ καταφιλήσει χεῖρας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν χρημάτων τοῦ πλησίον ταπεινώσει φωνήν

text_en: But when they should repay, they will ask time, and will return tedious and murmuring words, and will complain of the time:
text_la: et in tempore redditionis postulabit tempus, et loquetur verba tædii et murmurationum, et tempus causabitur.
text_el: καὶ ἐν καιρῷ ἀποδόσεως παρελκύσει χρόνον καὶ ἀποδώσει λόγους ἀκηδίας καὶ τὸν καιρὸν αἰτιάσεται

text_en: And if he be able to pay, he will stand off, he will scarce pay one half, and will count it as if he had found it:
text_la: Si autem potuerit reddere, adversabitur : solidi vix reddet dimidium, et computabit illud quasi inventionem :
text_el: ἐὰν ἰσχύσῃ μόλις κομίσεται τὸ ἥμισυ καὶ λογιεῖται αὐτὸ ὡς εὕρεμα

text_en: But if not, he will defraud him of his money, and he shall get him for an enemy without cause.
text_la: sin autem, fraudabit illum pecunia sua, et possidebit illum inimicum gratis :
text_el: εἰ δὲ μή ἀπεστέρησεν αὐτὸν τῶν χρημάτων αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκτήσατο αὐτὸν ἐχθρὸν δωρεάν

text_en: And he will pay him with reproaches and curses , and instead of honour and good turn will repay him injuries.
text_la: et convitia et maledicta reddet illi, et pro honore et beneficio reddet illi contumeliam.
text_el: κατάρας καὶ λοιδορίας ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ καὶ ἀντὶ δόξης ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ ἀτιμίαν

text_en: Many have refused to lend, not out of wickedness , but they were afraid to be defrauded without cause.
text_la: Multi non causa nequitiæ non fœnerati sunt, sed fraudari gratis timuerunt.
text_el: πολλοὶ οὐ χάριν πονηρίας ἀπέστρεψαν ἀποστερηθῆναι δωρεὰν εὐλαβήθησαν

text_en: But yet towards the poor be more hearty, and delay not to show him mercy.
text_la: Verumtamen super humilem animo fortior esto, et pro eleemosyna non trahas illum.
text_el: πλὴν ἐπὶ ταπεινῷ μακροθύμησον καὶ ἐπ' ἐλεημοσύνῃ μὴ παρελκύσῃς αὐτόν

text_en: Help the poor because of the commandment: and send him not away empty handed because of his poverty.
text_la: Propter mandatum assume pauperem, et propter inopiam ejus ne dimittas eum vacuum.
text_el: χάριν ἐντολῆς ἀντιλαβοῦ πένητος καὶ κατὰ τὴν ἔνδειαν αὐτοῦ μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς αὐτὸν κενόν

text_en: Lose your money for your brother and your friend: and hide it not under a stone to be lost.
text_la: Perde pecuniam propter fratrem et amicum tuum, et non abscondas illam sub lapide in perditionem.
text_el: ἀπόλεσον ἀργύριον δι' ἀδελφὸν καὶ φίλον καὶ μὴ ἰωθήτω ὑπὸ τὸν λίθον εἰς ἀπώλειαν

text_en: Place your treasure in the commandments of the most High , and it shall bring you more profit than gold.
text_la: Pone thesaurum tuum in præceptis Altissimi, et proderit tibi magis quam aurum.
text_el: θὲς τὸν θησαυρόν σου κατ' ἐντολὰς ὑψίστου καὶ λυσιτελήσει σοι μᾶλλον ἢ τὸ χρυσίον

text_en: Shut up alms in the heart of the poor, and it shall obtain help for you against all evil .
text_la: Conclude eleemosynam in corde pauperis, et hæc pro te exorabit ab omni malo.
text_el: σύγκλεισον ἐλεημοσύνην ἐν τοῖς ταμιείοις σου καὶ αὕτη ἐξελεῖταί σε ἐκ πάσης κακώσεως

text_en: Better than the shield of the mighty, and better than the spear: It shall fight for you against your enemy.
text_la: Super scutum potentis, et super lanceam : adversus inimicum tuum pugnabit.
text_el: ὑπὲρ ἀσπίδα κράτους καὶ ὑπὲρ δόρυ ὁλκῆς κατέναντι ἐχθροῦ πολεμήσει ὑπὲρ σοῦ

text_en: A good man is surety for his neighbour: and he that has lost shame, will leave him to himself.
text_la: Vir bonus fidem facit pro proximo suo : et qui perdiderit confusionem derelinquet sibi.
text_el: ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς ἐγγυήσεται τὸν πλησίον καὶ ὁ ἀπολωλεκὼς αἰσχύνην ἐγκαταλείψει αὐτόν

text_en: Forget not the kindness of your surety: for he has given his life for you.
text_la: Gratiam fidejussoris ne obliviscaris : dedit enim pro te animam suam.
text_el: χάριτας ἐγγύου μὴ ἐπιλάθῃ ἔδωκεν γὰρ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ὑπὲρ σοῦ

text_en: The sinner and the unclean flees from his surety.
text_la: Repromissorem fugit peccator et immundus.

text_en: A sinner attributes to himself the goods of his surety: and he that is of an unthankful mind will leave him that delivered him.
text_la: Bona repromissoris sibi ascribit peccator : et ingratus sensu derelinquet liberantem se.
text_el: ἀγαθὰ ἐγγύου ἀνατρέψει ἁμαρτωλός καὶ ἀχάριστος ἐν διανοίᾳ ἐγκαταλείψει ῥυσάμενον

text_en: A man is surety for his neighbour: and when he has lost all shame, he shall forsake him.
text_la: Vir repromittit de proximo suo : et cum perdiderit reverentiam, derelinquetur ab eo.

text_en: Evil suretyship has undone many of good estate, and has tossed them as a wave of the sea.
text_la: Repromissio nequissima multos perdidit dirigentes, et commovit illos quasi fluctus maris.
text_el: ἐγγύη πολλοὺς ἀπώλεσεν κατευθύνοντας καὶ ἐσάλευσεν αὐτοὺς ὡς κῦμα θαλάσσης

text_en: It has made powerful men to go from place to place round about, and they have wandered in strange countries.
text_la: Viros potentes gyrans migrare fecit, et vagati sunt in gentibus alienis.
text_el: ἄνδρας δυνατοὺς ἀπῴκισεν καὶ ἐπλανήθησαν ἐν ἔθνεσιν ἀλλοτρίοις

text_en: A sinner that transgresses the commandment of the Lord , shall fall into an evil suretyship: and he that undertakes many things, shall fall into judgment.
text_la: Peccator transgrediens mandatum Domini incidet in promissionem nequam : et qui conatur multa agere incidet in judicium.
text_el: ἁμαρτωλὸς ἐμπεσὼν εἰς ἐγγύην καὶ διώκων ἐργολαβίας ἐμπεσεῖται εἰς κρίσεις

text_en: Recover your neighbour according to your power, and take heed to yourself that you fall not.
text_la: Recupera proximum secundum virtutem tuam, et attende tibi ne incidas.
text_el: ἀντιλαβοῦ τοῦ πλησίον κατὰ δύναμίν σου καὶ πρόσεχε σεαυτῷ μὴ ἐμπέσῃς

text_en: The chief thing for man's life is water and bread, and clothing, and a house to cover shame.
text_la: Initium vitæ hominis, aqua et panis, et vestimentum, et domus protegens turpitudinem.
text_el: ἀρχὴ ζωῆς ὕδωρ καὶ ἄρτος καὶ ἱμάτιον καὶ οἶκος καλύπτων ἀσχημοσύνην

text_en: Better is the poor man's fare under a roof of boards, than sumptuous cheer abroad in another man's house.
text_la: Melior est victus pauperis sub tegmine asserum quam epulæ splendidæ in peregre sine domicilio.
text_el: κρείσσων βίος πτωχοῦ ὑπὸ σκέπην δοκῶν ἢ ἐδέσματα λαμπρὰ ἐν ἀλλοτρίοις

text_en: Be contented with little instead of much, and you shall not hear the reproach of going abroad.
text_la: Minimum pro magno placeat tibi, et improperium peregrinationis non audies.
text_el: ἐπὶ μικρῷ καὶ μεγάλῳ εὐδοκίαν ἔχε καὶ ὀνειδισμὸν παροικίας οὐ μὴ ἀκούσῃς

text_en: It is a miserable life to go as a guest from house to house: for where a man is a stranger, he shall not deal confidently, nor open his mouth.
text_la: Vita nequam hospitandi de domo in domum : et ubi hospitabitur non fiducialiter aget, nec aperiet os.
text_el: ζωὴ πονηρὰ ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν καὶ οὗ παροικήσεις οὐκ ἀνοίξεις στόμα

text_en: He shall entertain and feed, and give drink to the unthankful, and moreover he shall hear bitter words.
text_la: Hospitabitur, et pascet, et potabit ingratos, et ad hæc amara audiet :
text_el: ξενιεῖς καὶ ποτιεῖς εἰς ἀχάριστα καὶ πρὸς ἐπὶ τούτοις πικρὰ ἀκούσῃ

text_en: Go, stranger, and furnish the table, and give others to eat what you have in your hand.
text_la: transi, hospes, et orna mensam, et quæ in manu habes ciba ceteros.
text_el: πάρελθε πάροικε κόσμησον τράπεζαν καὶ εἴ τι ἐν τῇ χειρί σου ψώμισόν με

text_en: Give place to the honourable presence of my friends: for I want my house, my brother being to be lodged with me.
text_la: Exi a facie honoris amicorum meorum : necessitudine domus meæ hospitio mihi factus est frater.
text_el: ἔξελθε πάροικε ἀπὸ προσώπου δόξης ἐπεξένωταί μοι ὁ ἀδελφός χρεία τῆς οἰκίας

text_en: These things are grievous to a man of understanding: the upbraiding of houseroom, and the reproaching of the lender.
text_la: Gravia hæc homini habenti sensum : correptio domus, et improperium fœneratoris.
text_el: βαρέα ταῦτα ἀνθρώπῳ ἔχοντι φρόνησιν ἐπιτίμησις οἰκίας καὶ ὀνειδισμὸς δανειστοῦ

text_en: He that loves his son, frequently chastises him, that he may rejoice in his latter end, and not grope after the doors of his neighbours.
text_la: Qui diligit filium suum assiduat illi flagella, ut lætetur in novissimo suo, et non palpet proximorum ostia.
text_el: ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐνδελεχήσει μάστιγας αὐτῷ ἵνα εὐφρανθῇ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων αὐτοῦ

text_en: He that instructs his son shall be praised in him, and shall glory in him in the midst of them of his household.
text_la: Qui docet filium suum laudabitur in illo, et in medio domesticorum in illo gloriabitur.
text_el: ὁ παιδεύων τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ὀνήσεται ἐπ' αὐτῷ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον γνωρίμων ἐπ' αὐτῷ καυχήσεται

text_en: He that teaches his son, makes his enemy jealous, and in the midst of his friends he shall glory in him.
text_la: Qui docet filium suum in zelum mittit inimicum, et in medio amicorum gloriabitur in illo.
text_el: ὁ διδάσκων τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ παραζηλώσει τὸν ἐχθρὸν καὶ ἔναντι φίλων ἐπ' αὐτῷ ἀγαλλιάσεται

text_en: His father is dead, and he is as if he were not dead: for he has left one behind him that is like himself.
text_la: Mortuus est pater ejus, et quasi non est mortuus : similem enim reliquit sibi post se.
text_el: ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτοῦ ὁ πατήρ καὶ ὧς οὐκ ἀπέθανεν ὅμοιον γὰρ αὐτῷ κατέλιπεν μετ' αὐτόν

text_en: While he lived he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died he was not sorrowful, neither was he confounded before his enemies.
text_la: In vita sua vidit, et lætatus est in illo : in obitu suo non est contristatus, nec confusus est coram inimicis :
text_el: ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ εἶδεν καὶ εὐφράνθη καὶ ἐν τῇ τελευτῇ αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐλυπήθη

text_en: For he left behind him a defender of his house against his enemies, and one that will requite kindness to his friends.
text_la: reliquit enim defensorem domus contra inimicos, et amicis reddentem gratiam.
text_el: ἐναντίον ἐχθρῶν κατέλιπεν ἔκδικον καὶ τοῖς φίλοις ἀνταποδιδόντα χάριν

text_en: For the souls of his sons he shall bind up his wounds, and at every cry his bowels shall be troubled.
text_la: Pro animabus filiorum colligabit vulnera sua, et super omnem vocem turbabuntur viscera ejus.
text_el: περιψύχων υἱὸν καταδεσμεύσει τραύματα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ πάσῃ βοῇ ταραχθήσεται σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ

text_en: A horse not broken becomes stubborn, and a child left to himself will become headstrong.
text_la: Equus indomitus evadit durus, et filius remissus evadet præceps.
text_el: ἵππος ἀδάμαστος ἐκβαίνει σκληρός καὶ υἱὸς ἀνειμένος ἐκβαίνει προαλής

text_en: Give your son his way, and he shall make you afraid: play with him, and he shall make you sorrowful.
text_la: Lacta filium, et paventem te faciet : lude cum eo, et contristabit te.
text_el: τιθήνησον τέκνον καὶ ἐκθαμβήσει σε σύμπαιξον αὐτῷ καὶ λυπήσει σε

text_en: Laugh not with him, lest you have sorrow, and at the last your teeth be set on edge.
text_la: Non corrideas illi, ne doleas, et in novissimo obstupescent dentes tui.
text_el: μὴ συγγελάσῃς αὐτῷ ἵνα μὴ συνοδυνηθῇς καὶ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων γομφιάσεις τοὺς ὀδόντας σου

text_en: Give him not liberty in his youth, and wink not at his devices.
text_la: Non des illi potestatem in juventute, et ne despicias cogitatus illius.
text_el: μὴ δῷς αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν ἐν νεότητι

text_en: Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat his sides while he is a child, lest he grow stubborn, and regard you not, and so be a sorrow of heart to you.
text_la: Curva cervicem ejus in juventute, et tunde latera ejus dum infans est, ne forte induret, et non credat tibi, et erit tibi dolor animæ.
text_el: θλάσον τὰς πλευρὰς αὐτοῦ ὡς ἔστιν νήπιος μήποτε σκληρυνθεὶς ἀπειθήσῃ σοι

text_en: Instruct your son, and labour about him, lest his lewd behaviour be an offence to you.
text_la: Doce filium tuum, et operare in illo, ne in turpitudinem illius offendas.
text_el: παίδευσον τὸν υἱόν σου καὶ ἔργασαι ἐν αὐτῷ ἵνα μὴ ἐν τῇ ἀσχημοσύνῃ αὐτοῦ προσκόψῃς

text_en: Better is a poor man who is sound, and strong of constitution, than a rich man who is weak and afflicted with evils .
text_la: Melior est pauper sanus, et fortis viribus, quam dives imbecillis et flagellatus malitia.
text_el: κρείσσων πτωχὸς ὑγιὴς καὶ ἰσχύων τῇ ἕξει ἢ πλούσιος μεμαστιγωμένος εἰς σῶμα αὐτοῦ

text_en: Health of the soul in holiness of justice , is better than all gold and silver: and a sound body, than immense revenues.
text_la: Salus animæ in sanctitate justitiæ melior est omni auro et argento : et corpus validum quam census immensus.
text_el: ὑγίεια καὶ εὐεξία βελτίων παντὸς χρυσίου καὶ σῶμα εὔρωστον ἢ ὄλβος ἀμέτρητος

text_en: There is no riches above the riches of the health of the body: and there is no pleasure above the joy of the heart.
text_la: Non est census super censum salutis corporis, et non est oblectamentum super cordis gaudium.
text_el: οὐκ ἔστιν πλοῦτος βελτίων ὑγιείας σώματος καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν εὐφροσύνη ὑπὲρ χαρὰν καρδίας

text_en: Better is death than a bitter life, and everlasting rest, than continual sickness.
text_la: Melior est mors quam vita amara, et requies æterna quam languor perseverans.
text_el: κρείσσων θάνατος ὑπὲρ ζωὴν πικρὰν καὶ ἀνάπαυσις αἰῶνος ἢ ἀρρώστημα ἔμμονον

text_en: Good things that are hidden in a mouth that is shut, are as messes of meat set about a grave.
text_la: Bona abscondita in ore clauso, quasi appositiones epularum circumpositæ sepulchro.
text_el: ἀγαθὰ ἐκκεχυμένα ἐπὶ στόματι κεκλεισμένῳ θέματα βρωμάτων παρακείμενα ἐπὶ τάφῳ

text_en: What good shall an offering do to an idol ? For it can neither eat, nor smell:
text_la: Quid proderit libatio idolo? nec enim manducabit, nec odorabit.
text_el: τί συμφέρει κάρπωσις εἰδώλῳ οὔτε γὰρ ἔδεται οὔτε μὴ ὀσφρανθῇ

text_en: So is he that is persecuted by the Lord , bearing the reward of his iniquity :
text_la: Sic qui effugatur a Domino, portans mercedes iniquitatis :
text_el: οὕτως ὁ ἐκδιωκόμενος ὑπὸ κυρίου

text_en: He sees with his eyes, and groans, as an eunuch embracing a virgin , and sighing.
text_la: videns oculis et ingemiscens, sicut spado complectens virginem, et suspirans.
text_el: βλέπων ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ στενάζων ὥσπερ εὐνοῦχος περιλαμβάνων παρθένον καὶ στενάζων

text_en: Give not up your soul to sadness, and afflict not yourself in your own counsel.
text_la: Tristitiam non des animæ tuæ, et non affligas temetipsum in consilio tuo.
text_el: μὴ δῷς εἰς λύπην τὴν ψυχήν σου καὶ μὴ θλίψῃς σεαυτὸν ἐν βουλῇ σου

text_en: The joyfulness of the heart, is the life of a man , and a never failing treasure of holiness : and the joy of a man is length of life.
text_la: Jucunditas cordis, hæc est vita hominis, et thesaurus sine defectione sanctitatis : et exsultatio viri est longævitas.
text_el: εὐφροσύνη καρδίας ζωὴ ἀνθρώπου καὶ ἀγαλλίαμα ἀνδρὸς μακροημέρευσις

text_en: Have pity on your own soul , pleasing God , and contain yourself: gather up your heart in his holiness : and drive away sadness far from you.
text_la: Miserere animæ tuæ placens Deo, et contine : congrega cor tuum in sanctitate ejus, et tristitiam longe repelle a te.
text_el: ἀπάτα τὴν ψυχήν σου καὶ παρακάλει τὴν καρδίαν σου καὶ λύπην μακρὰν ἀπόστησον ἀπὸ σοῦ

text_en: For sadness has killed many, and there is no profit in it.
text_la: Multos enim occidit tristitia, et non est utilitas in illa.
text_el: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἀπώλεσεν ἡ λύπη καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ὠφέλεια ἐν αὐτῇ

text_en: Envy and anger shorten a man's days, and pensiveness will bring old age before the time.
text_la: Zelus et iracundia minuunt dies, et ante tempus senectam adducet cogitatus.
text_el: ζῆλος καὶ θυμὸς ἐλαττοῦσιν ἡμέρας καὶ πρὸ καιροῦ γῆρας ἄγει μέριμνα

text_en: A cheerful and good heart is always feasting: for his banquets are prepared with diligence.
text_la: Splendidum cor et bonum in epulis est : epulæ enim illius diligenter fiunt.
text_el: λαμπρὰ καρδία καὶ ἀγαθὴ ἐπὶ ἐδέσμασιν τῶν βρωμάτων αὐτῆς ἐπιμελήσεται

text_en: Watching for riches consumes the flesh, and the thought thereof drives away sleep.
text_la: Vigilia honestatis tabefaciet carnes, et cogitatus illius auferet somnum.
text_el: ἀγρυπνία πλούτου ἐκτήκει σάρκας καὶ ἡ μέριμνα αὐτοῦ ἀφιστᾷ ὕπνον

text_en: The thinking beforehand turns away the understanding, and a grievous sickness makes the soul sober.
text_la: Cogitatus præscientiæ avertit sensum, et infirmitas gravis sobriam facit animam.
text_el: μέριμνα ἀγρυπνίας ἀποστήσει νυσταγμόν καὶ ἀρρώστημα βαρὺ ἐκνήψει ὕπνον

text_en: The rich man has laboured in gathering riches together, and when he rests he shall be filled with his goods.
text_la: Laboravit dives in congregatione substantiæ, et in requie sua replebitur bonis suis.
text_el: ἐκοπίασεν πλούσιος ἐν συναγωγῇ χρημάτων καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀναπαύσει ἐμπίμπλαται τῶν τρυφημάτων αὐτοῦ

text_en: The poor man has laboured in his low way of life, and in the end he is still poor.
text_la: Laboravit pauper in diminutione victus, et in fine inops fit.
text_el: ἐκοπίασεν πτωχὸς ἐν ἐλαττώσει βίου καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀναπαύσει ἐπιδεὴς γίνεται

text_en: He that loves gold, shall not be justified: and he that follows after corruption, shall be filled with it.
text_la: Qui aurum diligit non justificabitur, et qui insequitur consumptionem replebitur ex ea.
text_el: ὁ ἀγαπῶν χρυσίον οὐ δικαιωθήσεται καὶ ὁ διώκων διάφορα ἐν αὐτοῖς πλανηθήσεται

text_en: Many have been brought to fall for gold, and the beauty thereof has been their ruin.
text_la: Multi dati sunt in auri casus, et facta est in specie ipsius perditio illorum.
text_el: πολλοὶ ἐδόθησαν εἰς πτῶμα χάριν χρυσίου καὶ ἐγενήθη ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν

text_en: Gold is a stumbling block to them that sacrifice to it: woe to them that eagerly follow after it, and every fool shall perish by it.
text_la: Lignum offensionis est aurum sacrificantium : væ illis qui sectantur illud! et omnis imprudens deperiet in illo.
text_el: ξύλον προσκόμματός ἐστιν τοῖς ἐνθουσιάζουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ πᾶς ἄφρων ἁλώσεται ἐν αὐτῷ

text_en: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that has not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures.
text_la: Beatus dives qui inventus est sine macula, et qui post aurum non abiit, nec speravit in pecunia et thesauris.
text_el: μακάριος πλούσιος ὃς εὑρέθη ἄμωμος καὶ ὃς ὀπίσω χρυσίου οὐκ ἐπορεύθη

text_en: Who is he, and we will praise him? For he has done wonderful things in his life.
text_la: Quis est hic? et laudabimus eum : fecit enim mirabilia in vita sua.
text_el: τίς ἐστιν καὶ μακαριοῦμεν αὐτόν ἐποίησεν γὰρ θαυμάσια ἐν λαῷ αὐτοῦ

text_en: Who has been tried thereby, and made perfect, he shall have glory everlasting. He that could have transgressed, and has not transgressed: and could do evil things, and has not done them:
text_la: Qui probatus est in illo, et perfectus est, erit illi gloria æterna : qui potuit transgredi, et non est transgressus; facere mala, et non fecit.
text_el: τίς ἐδοκιμάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐτελειώθη καὶ ἔσται αὐτῷ εἰς καύχησιν τίς ἐδύνατο παραβῆναι καὶ οὐ παρέβη καὶ ποιῆσαι κακὰ καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν

text_en: Therefore are his goods established in the Lord , and all the church of the saints shall declare his alms .
text_la: Ideo stabilita sunt bona illius in Domino, et eleemosynas illius enarrabit omnis ecclesia sanctorum.
text_el: στερεωθήσεται τὰ ἀγαθὰ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς ἐλεημοσύνας αὐτοῦ ἐκδιηγήσεται ἐκκλησία

text_en: Are you set at a great table? Be not the first to open your mouth upon it.
text_la: Supra mensam magnam sedisti? non aperias super illam faucem tuam prior.
text_el: ἐπὶ τραπέζης μεγάλης ἐκάθισας μὴ ἀνοίξῃς ἐπ' αὐτῆς φάρυγγά σου

text_en: Say not: There are many things which are upon it.
text_la: Non dicas sic : Multa sunt, quæ super illam sunt.
text_el: καὶ μὴ εἴπῃς πολλά γε τὰ ἐπ' αὐτῆς

text_en: Remember that a wicked eye is evil .
text_la: Memento quoniam malus est oculus nequam.
text_el: μνήσθητι ὅτι κακὸν ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός

text_en: What is created more wicked than an eye? Therefore shall it weep over all the face when it shall see.
text_la: Nequius oculo quid creatum est? ideo ab omni facie sua lacrimabitur, cum viderit.
text_el: πονηρότερον ὀφθαλμοῦ τί ἔκτισται διὰ τοῦτο ἀπὸ παντὸς προσώπου δακρύει

text_en: Stretch not out your hand first, lest being disgraced with envy you be put to confusion.
text_la: Ne extendas manum tuam prior, et invidia contaminatus erubescas.
text_el: οὗ ἐὰν ἐπιβλέψῃ μὴ ἐκτείνῃς χεῖρα

text_en: Be not hasty in a feast.
text_la: Ne comprimaris in convivio.
text_el: καὶ μὴ συνθλίβου αὐτῷ ἐν τρυβλίῳ

text_en: Judge of the disposition of your neighbour by yourself.
text_la: Intellige quæ sunt proximi tui ex teipso.
text_el: νόει τὰ τοῦ πλησίον ἐκ σεαυτοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ παντὶ πράγματι διανοοῦ

text_en: Use as a frugal man the things that are set before you: lest if you eat much, you be hated .
text_la: Utere quasi homo frugi his quæ tibi apponuntur : ne, cum manducas multum, odio habearis.
text_el: φάγε ὡς ἄνθρωπος τὰ παρακείμενά σοι καὶ μὴ διαμασῶ μὴ μισηθῇς

text_en: Leave off first, for manners' sake: and exceed not, lest you offend.
text_la: Cessa prior causa disciplinæ : et noli nimius esse, ne forte offendas.
text_el: παῦσαι πρῶτος χάριν παιδείας καὶ μὴ ἀπληστεύου μήποτε προσκόψῃς

text_en: And if you sit among many, reach not your hand out first of all, and be not the first to ask for drink.
text_la: Et si in medio multorum sedisti, prior illis ne extendas manum tuam, nec prior poscas bibere.
text_el: καὶ εἰ ἀνὰ μέσον πλειόνων ἐκάθισας πρότερος αὐτῶν μὴ ἐκτείνῃς τὴν χεῖρά σου

text_en: How sufficient is a little wine for a man well taught, and in sleeping you shall not be uneasy with it, and you shall feel no pain.
text_la: Quam sufficiens est homini eruditio vinum exiguum! et in dormiendo non laborabis ab illo, et non senties dolorem.
text_el: ὡς ἱκανὸν ἀνθρώπῳ πεπαιδευμένῳ τὸ ὀλίγον καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κοίτης αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀσθμαίνει

text_en: Watching, and choler, and gripes, are with an intemperate man :
text_la: Vigilia, cholera et tortura viro infrunito,
text_el: πόνος ἀγρυπνίας καὶ χολέρας καὶ στρόφος μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἀπλήστου

text_en: Sound and wholesome sleep with a moderate man : he shall sleep till morning, and his soul shall be delighted with him.
text_la: somnus sanitatis in homine parco : dormiet usque mane, et anima illius cum ipso delectabitur.
text_el: ὕπνος ὑγιείας ἐπὶ ἐντέρῳ μετρίῳ ἀνέστη πρωί καὶ ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ μετ' αὐτοῦ

text_en: And if you have been forced to eat much, arise, go out, and vomit: and it shall refresh you, and you shall not bring sickness upon your body.
text_la: Et si coactus fueris in edendo multum, surge e medio, evome, et refrigerabit te, et non adduces corpori tuo infirmitatem.
text_el: καὶ εἰ ἐβιάσθης ἐν ἐδέσμασιν ἀνάστα ἔμεσον πόρρω καὶ ἀναπαύσῃ

text_en: Hear me, my son, and despise me not: and in the end you shall find my words.
text_la: Audi me, fili, et ne spernas me, et in novissimo invenies verba mea.
text_el: ἄκουσόν μου τέκνον καὶ μὴ ἐξουδενήσῃς με καὶ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων εὑρήσεις τοὺς λόγους μου

text_en: In all your works be quick, and no infirmity shall come to you.
text_la: In omnibus operibus tuis esto velox, et omnis infirmitas non occurret tibi.
text_el: ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἔργοις σου γίνου ἐντρεχής καὶ πᾶν ἀρρώστημα οὐ μή σοι ἀπαντήσῃ

text_en: The lips of many shall bless him that is liberal of his bread, and the testimony of his truth is faithful.
text_la: Splendidum in panibus benedicent labia multorum, et testimonium veritatis illius fidele.
text_el: λαμπρὸν ἐπ' ἄρτοις εὐλογήσει χείλη καὶ ἡ μαρτυρία τῆς καλλονῆς αὐτοῦ πιστή

text_en: Against him that is niggardly of his bread, the city will murmur, and the testimony of his niggardliness is true .
text_la: Nequissimo in pane murmurabit civitas, et testimonium nequitiæ illius verum est.
text_el: πονηρῷ ἐπ' ἄρτῳ διαγογγύσει πόλις καὶ ἡ μαρτυρία τῆς πονηρίας αὐτοῦ ἀκριβής

text_en: Challenge not them that love wine: for wine has destroyed very many.
text_la: Diligentes in vino noli provocare : multos enim exterminavit vinum.
text_el: ἐν οἴνῳ μὴ ἀνδρίζου πολλοὺς γὰρ ἀπώλεσεν ὁ οἶνος

text_en: Fire tries hard iron: so wine drunk to excess shall rebuke the hearts of the proud .
text_la: Ignis probat ferrum durum : sic vinum corda superborum arguet in ebrietate potatum.
text_el: κάμινος δοκιμάζει στόμωμα ἐν βαφῇ οὕτως οἶνος καρδίας ἐν μάχῃ ὑπερηφάνων

text_en: Wine taken with sobriety is equal life to men : if you drink it moderately, you shall be sober.
text_la: Æqua vita hominibus vinum in sobrietate : si bibas illud moderate, eris sobrius.
text_el: ἔφισον ζωῆς οἶνος ἀνθρώποις ἐὰν πίνῃς αὐτὸν ἐν μέτρῳ αὐτοῦ

text_en: What is his life, who is diminished with wine?
text_la: Quæ vita est ei qui minuitur vino?
text_el: τίς ζωὴ ἐλασσουμένῳ οἴνῳ

text_en: What takes away life? Death.
text_la: Quid defraudat vitam? mors.

text_en: Wine was created from the beginning to make men joyful, and not to make them drunk.
text_la: Vinum in jucunditatem creatum est, et non in ebrietatem ab initio.
text_el: καὶ αὐτὸς ἔκτισται εἰς εὐφροσύνην ἀνθρώποις

text_en: Wine drunken with moderation is the joy of the soul and the heart.
text_la: Exsultatio animæ et cordis vinum moderate potatum.
text_el: ἀγαλλίαμα καρδίας καὶ εὐφροσύνη ψυχῆς οἶνος πινόμενος ἐν καιρῷ αὐτάρκης

text_en: Sober drinking is health to soul and body.
text_la: Sanitas est animæ et corpori sobrius potus.

text_en: Wine drunken with excess raises quarrels, and wrath , and many ruins.
text_la: Vinum multum potatum irritationem, et iram, et ruinas multas facit.
text_el: πικρία ψυχῆς οἶνος πινόμενος πολὺς ἐν ἐρεθισμῷ καὶ ἀντιπτώματι

text_en: Wine drunken with excess is bitterness of the soul .
text_la: Amaritudo animæ vinum multum potatum.

text_en: The heat of drunkenness is the stumbling block of the fool, lessening strength and causing wounds.
text_la: Ebrietatis animositas, imprudentis offensio, minorans virtutem, et faciens vulnera.
text_el: πληθύνει μέθη θυμὸν ἄφρονος εἰς πρόσκομμα ἐλαττῶν ἰσχὺν καὶ προσποιῶν τραύματα

text_en: Rebuke not your neighbour in a banquet of wine: and despise him not in his mirth.
text_la: In convivio vini non arguas proximum, et non despicias eum in jucunditate illius.
text_el: ἐν συμποσίῳ οἴνου μὴ ἐλέγξῃς τὸν πλησίον καὶ μὴ ἐξουθενήσῃς αὐτὸν ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ αὐτοῦ

text_en: Speak not to him words of reproach: and press him not in demanding again.
text_la: Verba improperii non dicas illi, et non premas illum repetendo.
text_el: λόγον ὀνειδισμοῦ μὴ εἴπῃς αὐτῷ καὶ μὴ αὐτὸν θλίψῃς ἐν ἀπαιτήσει

text_en: Have they made you ruler? Be not lifted up: be among them as one of them.
text_la: Rectorem te posuerunt? noli extolli : esto in illis quasi unus ex ipsis.
text_el: ἡγούμενόν σε κατέστησαν μὴ ἐπαίρου γίνου ἐν αὐτοῖς ὡς εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν

text_en: Have care of them, and so sit down, and when you have acquitted yourself of all your charge, take your place:
text_la: Curam illorum habe, et sic conside, et omni cura tua explicita recumbe :
text_el: φρόντισον αὐτῶν καὶ οὕτω κάθισον καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν χρείαν σου ποιήσας ἀνάπεσε

text_en: That you may rejoice for them, and receive a crown as an ornament of grace , and get the honour of the contribution.
text_la: ut læteris propter illos, et ornamentum gratiæ accipias coronam, et dignationem consequaris corrogationis.
text_el: ἵνα εὐφρανθῇς δι' αὐτοὺς καὶ εὐκοσμίας χάριν λάβῃς στέφανον

text_en: Speak, you that are elder: for it becomes you,
text_la: Loquere major natu: decet enim te
text_el: λάλησον πρεσβύτερε πρέπει γάρ σοι

text_en: to speak the first word with careful knowledge , and hinder not music.
text_la: primum verbum diligenti scientia, et non impedias musicam.
text_el: ἐν ἀκριβεῖ ἐπιστήμῃ καὶ μὴ ἐμποδίσῃς μουσικά

text_en: Where there is no hearing, pour not out words, and be not lifted up out of season with your wisdom.
text_la: Ubi auditus non est, non effundas sermonem, et importune noli extolli in sapientia tua.
text_el: ὅπου ἀκρόαμα μὴ ἐκχέῃς λαλιὰν καὶ ἀκαίρως μὴ σοφίζου

text_en: A concert of music in a banquet of wine is as a carbuncle set in gold.
text_la: Gemmula carbunculi in ornamento auri, et comparatio musicorum in convivio vini.
text_el: σφραγὶς ἄνθρακος ἐπὶ κόσμῳ χρυσῷ σύγκριμα μουσικῶν ἐν συμποσίῳ οἴνου

text_en: As a signet of an emerald in a work of gold: so is the melody of music with pleasant and moderate wine.
text_la: Sicut in fabricatione auri signum est smaragdi, sic numerus musicorum in jucundo et moderato vino.
text_el: ἐν κατασκευάσματι χρυσῷ σφραγὶς σμαράγδου μέλος μουσικῶν ἐφ' ἡδεῖ οἴνῳ

text_en: Hear in silence, and for your reverence good grace shall come to you.
text_la: Audi tacens, et pro reverentia accedet tibi bona gratia.

text_en: Young man , scarcely speak in your own cause.
text_la: Adolescens, loquere in tua causa vix.
text_el: λάλησον νεανίσκε εἰ χρεία σου μόλις

text_en: If you be asked twice, let your answer be short.
text_la: Si bis interrogatus fueris, habeat caput responsum tuum.
text_el: δὶς ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇς κεφαλαίωσον λόγον

text_en: In many things be as if you were ignorant , and hear in silence and withal seeking.
text_la: In multis esto quasi inscius, et audi tacens simul et quærens.
text_el: ἐν ὀλίγοις πολλά γίνου ὡς γινώσκων καὶ ἅμα σιωπῶν

text_en: In the company of great men take not upon you: and when the ancients are present, speak not much.
text_la: In medio magnatorum non præsumas : et ubi sunt senes non multum loquaris.
text_el: ἐν μέσῳ μεγιστάνων μὴ ἐξισάζου καὶ ἑτέρου λέγοντος μὴ πολλὰ ἀδολέσχει

text_en: Before a storm goes lightning: and before shamefacedness goes favour: and for your reverence good grace shall come to you.
text_la: Ante grandinem præibit coruscatio : et ante verecundiam præibit gratia, et pro reverentia accedet tibi bona gratia.
text_el: πρὸ βροντῆς κατασπεύδει ἀστραπή καὶ πρὸ αἰσχυντηροῦ προελεύσεται χάρις

text_en: And at the time of rising be not slack: but be first to run home to your house, and there withdraw yourself, and there take your pastime.
text_la: Et hora surgendi non te trices : præcurre autem prior in domum tuam, et illic avocare, et illic lude,
text_el: ἐν ὥρᾳ ἐξεγείρου καὶ μὴ οὐράγει ἀπότρεχε εἰς οἶκον καὶ μὴ ῥᾳθύμει ἐκεῖ παῖζε

text_en: And do what you have a mind, but not in sin or proud speech.
text_la: et age conceptiones tuas, et non in delictis et verbo superbo :
text_el: καὶ ποίει τὰ ἐνθυμήματά σου καὶ μὴ ἁμάρτῃς λόγῳ ὑπερηφάνῳ

text_en: And for all these things bless the Lord , that made you, and that replenishes you with all his good things.
text_la: et super his omnibus benedicito Dominum, qui fecit, et inebriantem te ab omnibus bonis suis.
text_el: καὶ ἐπὶ τούτοις εὐλόγησον τὸν ποιήσαντά σε καὶ μεθύσκοντά σε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀγαθῶν αὐτοῦ

text_en: He that fears the Lord , will receive his discipline: and they that will seek him early, shall find a blessing .
text_la: Qui timet Dominum excipiet doctrinam ejus : et qui vigilaverint ad illum invenient benedictionem.
text_el: ὁ φοβούμενος κύριον ἐκδέξεται παιδείαν καὶ οἱ ὀρθρίζοντες εὑρήσουσιν εὐδοκίαν

text_en: He that seeks the law, shall be filled with it: and he that deals deceitfully, shall meet with a stumbling block therein.
text_la: Qui quærit legem replebitur ab ea, et qui insidiose agit scandalizabitur in ea.
text_el: ὁ ζητῶν νόμον ἐμπλησθήσεται αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ ὑποκρινόμενος σκανδαλισθήσεται ἐν αὐτῷ

text_en: They that fear the Lord , shall find just judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.
text_la: Qui timent Dominum invenient judicium justum, et justitias quasi lumen accendent.
text_el: οἱ φοβούμενοι κύριον εὑρήσουσιν κρίμα καὶ δικαιώματα ὡς φῶς ἐξάψουσιν

text_en: A sinful man will flee reproof, and will find an excuse according to his will.
text_la: Peccator homo vitabit correptionem, et secundum voluntatem suam inveniet comparationem.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλὸς ἐκκλινεῖ ἐλεγμὸν καὶ κατὰ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει σύγκριμα

text_en: A man of counsel will not neglect understanding, a strange and proud man will not dread fear:
text_la: Vir consilii non disperdet intelligentiam : alienus et superbus non pertimescet timorem :
text_el: ἀνὴρ βουλῆς οὐ μὴ παρίδῃ διανόημα ἀλλότριος καὶ ὑπερήφανος οὐ καταπτήξει φόβον

text_en: Even after he has done with fear without counsel, he shall be controlled by the things of his own seeking.
text_la: etiam postquam fecit cum eo sine consilio, et suis insectationibus arguetur.

text_en: My son, do nothing without counsel, and you shall not repent when you have done.
text_la: Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis.
text_el: ἄνευ βουλῆς μηθὲν ποιήσῃς καὶ ἐν τῷ ποιῆσαί σε μὴ μεταμελοῦ

text_en: Go not in the way of ruin, and you shall not stumble against the stones: trust not yourself to a rugged way, lest you set a stumbling block to your soul .
text_la: In via ruinæ non eas, et non offendes in lapides : nec credas te viæ laboriosæ, ne ponas animæ tuæ scandalum.
text_el: ἐν ὁδῷ ἀντιπτώματος μὴ πορεύου καὶ μὴ προσκόψῃς ἐν λιθώδεσιν μὴ πιστεύσῃς ἐν ὁδῷ ἀπροσκόπῳ

text_en: And beware of your own children, and take heed of them of your household.
text_la: Et a filiis tuis cave, et a domesticis tuis attende.
text_el: καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν τέκνων σου φύλαξαι

text_en: In every work of yours regard your soul in faith : for this is the keeping of the commandments.
text_la: In omni opere tuo crede ex fide animæ tuæ, hoc est enim conservatio mandatorum.
text_el: ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ πίστευε τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ γὰρ τοῦτό ἐστιν τήρησις ἐντολῶν

text_en: He that believes God , takes heed to the commandments: and he that trusts in him, shall fare never the worse.
text_la: Qui credit Deo attendit mandatis : et qui confidit in illo non minorabitur.
text_el: ὁ πιστεύων νόμῳ προσέχει ἐντολαῖς καὶ ὁ πεποιθὼς κυρίῳ οὐκ ἐλαττωθήσεται

text_en: No evils shall happen to him that fears the Lord , but in temptation God will keep him and deliver him from evils .
text_la: Timenti Dominum non occurrent mala : sed in tentatione Deus illum conservabit, et liberabit a malis. Sapiens non odit mandata et justitias,
text_el: τῷ φοβουμένῳ κύριον οὐκ ἀπαντήσει κακόν ἀλλ' ἐν πειρασμῷ καὶ πάλιν ἐξελεῖται

text_en: A wise man hates not the commandments and justices, and he shall not be dashed in pieces as a ship in a storm.
text_la: et non illidetur quasi in procella navis.
text_el: ἀνὴρ σοφὸς οὐ μισήσει νόμον ὁ δὲ ὑποκρινόμενος ἐν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐν καταιγίδι πλοῖον

text_en: A man of understanding is faithful to the law of God , and the law is faithful to him.
text_la: Homo sensatus credit legi Dei, et lex illi fidelis.
text_el: ἄνθρωπος συνετὸς ἐμπιστεύσει νόμῳ καὶ ὁ νόμος αὐτῷ πιστὸς

text_en: He that clears up a question, shall prepare what to say, and so having prayed he shall be heard, and shall keep discipline, and then he shall answer.
text_la: Qui interrogationem manifestat parabit verbum, et sic deprecatus exaudietur : et conservabit disciplinam, et tunc respondebit.
text_el: ὡς ἐρώτημα δήλων ἑτοίμασον λόγον καὶ οὕτως ἀκουσθήσῃ σύνδησον παιδείαν καὶ ἀποκρίθητι

text_en: The heart of a fool is as a wheel of a cart: and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.
text_la: Præcordia fatui quasi rota carri, et quasi axis versatilis cogitatus illius.
text_el: τροχὸς ἁμάξης σπλάγχνα μωροῦ καὶ ὡς ἄξων στρεφόμενος ὁ διαλογισμὸς αὐτοῦ

text_en: A friend that is a mocker, is like a stallion horse: he neighs under every one that sits upon him.
text_la: Equus emissarius, sic et amicus subsannator : sub omni supra sedente hinnit.
text_el: ἵππος εἰς ὀχείαν ὡς φίλος μωκός ὑποκάτω παντὸς ἐπικαθημένου χρεμετίζει

text_en: Why does one day excel another, and one light another, and one year another year, when all come of the sun?
text_la: Quare dies diem superat, et iterum lux lucem, et annus annum a sole?
text_el: διὰ τί ἡμέρα ἡμέρας ὑπερέχει καὶ πᾶν φῶς ἡμέρας ἐνιαυτοῦ ἀφ' ἡλίου

text_en: By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished, the sun being made, and keeping his commandment.
text_la: A Domini scientia separati sunt, facto sole, et præceptum custodiente.
text_el: ἐν γνώσει κυρίου διεχωρίσθησαν

text_en: And he ordered the seasons, and holidays of them, and in them they celebrated festivals at an hour.
text_la: Et immutavit tempora, et dies festos ipsorum, et in illis dies festos celebraverunt ad horam.
text_el: καὶ ἠλλοίωσεν καιροὺς καὶ ἑορτάς

text_en: Some of them God made high and great days, and some of them he put in the number of ordinary days. And all men are from the ground, and out of the earth, from whence Adam was created .
text_la: Ex ipsis exaltavit et magnificavit Deus, et ex ipsis posuit in numerum dierum : et omnes homines de solo et ex terra unde creatus est Adam.
text_el: ἀπ' αὐτῶν ἀνύψωσεν καὶ ἡγίασεν καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἔθηκεν εἰς ἀριθμὸν ἡμερῶν καὶ ἄνθρωποι πάντες ἀπὸ ἐδάφους καὶ ἐκ γῆς ἐκτίσθη Αδαμ

text_en: With much knowledge the Lord has divided them and diversified their ways.
text_la: In multitudine disciplinæ Dominus separavit eos, et immutavit vias eorum.
text_el: ἐν πλήθει ἐπιστήμης κύριος διεχώρισεν αὐτοὺς καὶ ἠλλοίωσεν τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν

text_en: Some of them has he blessed , and exalted: and some of them has he sanctified , and set near himself: and some of them has he cursed and brought low, and turned them from their station.
text_la: Ex ipsis benedixit et exaltavit, et ex ipsis sanctificavit, et ad se applicavit, et ex ipsis maledixit, et humiliavit, et convertit illos a separatione ipsorum.
text_el: ἐξ αὐτῶν εὐλόγησεν καὶ ἀνύψωσεν καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἡγίασεν καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἤγγισεν ἀπ' αὐτῶν κατηράσατο καὶ ἐταπείνωσεν καὶ ἀνέστρεψεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ στάσεως αὐτῶν

text_en: As the potter's clay is in his hand, to fashion and order it:
text_la: Quasi lutum figuli in manu ipsius, plasmare illud et disponere.
text_el: ὡς πηλὸς κεραμέως ἐν χειρὶ αὐτοῦ

text_en: All his ways are according to his ordering: so man is in the hand of him that made him, and he will render to him according to his judgment.
text_la: Omnes viæ ejus secundum dispositionem ejus : sic homo in manu illius qui se fecit, et reddet illi secundum judicium suum.
text_el: πᾶσαι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν αὐτοῦ οὕτως ἄνθρωποι ἐν χειρὶ τοῦ ποιήσαντος αὐτοὺς ἀποδοῦναι αὐτοῖς κατὰ τὴν κρίσιν αὐτοῦ

text_en: Good is set against evil , and life against death: so also is the sinner against a just man . And so look upon all the works of the most High . Two and two, and one against another.
text_la: Contra malum bonum est, et contra mortem vita : sic et contra virum justum peccator, et sic intuere in omnia opera Altissimi, duo et duo, et unum contra unum.
text_el: ἀπέναντι τοῦ κακοῦ τὸ ἀγαθόν καὶ ἀπέναντι τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ζωή οὕτως ἀπέναντι εὐσεβοῦς ἁμαρτωλός καὶ οὕτως ἔμβλεψον εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ὑψίστου δύο δύο ἓν κατέναντι τοῦ ἑνός

text_en: And I awaked last of all, and as one that gathers after the grapegatherers.
text_la: Et ego novissimus evigilavi, et quasi qui colligit acinos post vindemiatores.
text_el: κἀγὼ ἔσχατος ἠγρύπνησα ὡς καλαμώμενος ὀπίσω τρυγητῶν

text_en: In the blessing of God I also have hoped: and as one that gathers grapes, have I filled the winepress.
text_la: In benedictione Dei et ipse speravi, et quasi qui vindemiat replevi torcular.
text_el: ἐν εὐλογίᾳ κυρίου ἔφθασα καὶ ὡς τρυγῶν ἐπλήρωσα ληνόν

text_en: See that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all that seek discipline.
text_la: Respicite quoniam non mihi soli laboravi, sed omnibus exquirentibus disciplinam.
text_el: κατανοήσατε ὅτι οὐκ ἐμοὶ μόνῳ ἐκοπίασα ἀλλὰ πᾶσιν τοῖς ζητοῦσιν παιδείαν

text_en: Hear me, you great men , and all you people, and hearken with your ears, you rulers of the church .
text_la: Audite me, magnates et omnes populi : et rectores ecclesiæ, auribus percipite.
text_el: ἀκούσατέ μου μεγιστᾶνες λαοῦ καὶ οἱ ἡγούμενοι ἐκκλησίας ἐνωτίσασθε

text_en: Give not to son or wife, brother or friend, power over you while you live; and give not your estate to another, lest you repent, and you entreat for the same.
text_la: Filio et mulieri, fratri et amico, non des potestatem super te in vita tua : et non dederis alii possessionem tuam, ne forte pœniteat te, et depreceris pro illis.
text_el: υἱῷ καὶ γυναικί ἀδελφῷ καὶ φίλῳ μὴ δῷς ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ σὲ ἐν ζωῇ σου καὶ μὴ δῷς ἑτέρῳ τὰ χρήματά σου ἵνα μὴ μεταμεληθεὶς δέῃ περὶ αὐτῶν

text_en: As long as you live, and have breath in you, let no man change you.
text_la: Dum adhuc superes et aspiras, non immutabit te omnis caro.
text_el: ἕως ἔτι ζῇς καὶ πνοὴ ἐν σοί μὴ ἀλλάξῃς σεαυτὸν ἐν πάσῃ σαρκί

text_en: For it is better that your children should ask of you, than that you look toward the hands of your children.
text_la: Melius est enim ut filii tui te rogent, quam te respicere in manus filiorum tuorum.
text_el: κρεῖσσον γάρ ἐστιν τὰ τέκνα δεηθῆναί σου ἢ σὲ ἐμβλέπειν εἰς χεῖρας υἱῶν σου

text_en: In all your works keep the pre-eminence.
text_la: In omnibus operibus tuis præcellens esto.
text_el: ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἔργοις σου γίνου ὑπεράγων

text_en: Let no stain sully your glory . In the time when you shall end the days of your life, and in the time of your decease, distribute your inheritance.
text_la: Ne dederis maculam in gloria tua. In die consummationis dierum vitæ tuæ, et in tempore exitus tui, distribue hæreditatem tuam.
text_el: μὴ δῷς μῶμον ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ συντελείας ἡμερῶν ζωῆς σου καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τελευτῆς διάδος κληρονομίαν

text_en: Fodder, and a wand, and a burden are for an ass: bread, and correction, and work for a slave.
text_la: Cibaria, et virga, et onus asino : panis, et disciplina, et opus servo.
text_el: χορτάσματα καὶ ῥάβδος καὶ φορτία ὄνῳ ἄρτος καὶ παιδεία καὶ ἔργον οἰκέτῃ

text_en: He works under correction, and seeks to rest: let his hands be idle, and he seeks liberty.
text_la: Operatur in disciplina, et quærit requiescere : laxa manus illi, et quærit libertatem.
text_el: ἔργασαι ἐν παιδί καὶ εὑρήσεις ἀνάπαυσιν ἄνες χεῖρας αὐτῷ καὶ ζητήσει ἐλευθερίαν

text_en: The yoke and the thong bend a stiff neck, and continual labours bow a slave.
text_la: Jugum et lorum curvant collum durum, et servum inclinant operationes assiduæ.
text_el: ζυγὸς καὶ ἱμὰς τράχηλον κάμψουσιν

text_en: Torture and fetters are for a malicious slave: send him to work, that he be not idle:
text_la: Servo malevolo tortura et compedes : mitte illum in operationem, ne vacet :
text_el: καὶ οἰκέτῃ κακούργῳ στρέβλαι καὶ βάσανοι ἔμβαλε αὐτὸν εἰς ἐργασίαν ἵνα μὴ ἀργῇ

text_en: For idleness has taught much evil .
text_la: multam enim malitiam docuit otiositas.
text_el: πολλὴν γὰρ κακίαν ἐδίδαξεν ἡ ἀργία

text_en: Set him to work: for so it is fit for him. And if he be not obedient , bring him down with fetters, but be not excessive towards any one, and do no grievous thing without judgment.
text_la: In opera constitue eum : sic enim condecet illum. Quod si non obaudierit, curva illum compedibus, et non amplifices super omnem carnem : verum sine judicio nihil facias grave.
text_el: εἰς ἔργα κατάστησον καθὼς πρέπει αὐτῷ κἂν μὴ πειθαρχῇ βάρυνον τὰς πέδας αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ περισσεύσῃς ἐπὶ πάσῃ σαρκὶ καὶ ἄνευ κρίσεως μὴ ποιήσῃς μηδέν

text_en: If you have a faithful servant, let him be to you as your own soul : treat him as a brother: because in the blood of your soul you have gotten him.
text_la: Si est tibi servus fidelis, sit tibi quasi anima tua : quasi fratrem sic eum tracta, quoniam in sanguine animæ comparasti illum.
text_el: εἰ ἔστιν σοι οἰκέτης ἔστω ὡς σύ ὅτι ἐν αἵματι ἐκτήσω αὐτόν εἰ ἔστιν σοι οἰκέτης ἄγε αὐτὸν ὡς ἀδελφόν ὅτι ὡς ἡ ψυχή σου ἐπιδεήσεις αὐτῷ

text_en: If you hurt him unjustly , he will run away:
text_la: Si læseris eum injuste, in fugam convertetur :
text_el: ἐὰν κακώσῃς αὐτὸν

text_en: And if he rise up and depart, you know not whom to ask, and in what way to seek him.
text_la: et si extollens discesserit, quem quæras et in qua via quæras illum nescis.
text_el: καὶ ἀπάρας ἀποδρᾷ ἐν ποίᾳ ὁδῷ ζητήσεις αὐτόν

text_en: The hopes of a man that is void of understanding are vain and deceitful: and dreams lift up fools.
text_la: Vana spes et mendacium viro insensato : et somnia extollunt imprudentes.
text_el: κεναὶ ἐλπίδες καὶ ψευδεῖς ἀσυνέτῳ ἀνδρί καὶ ἐνύπνια ἀναπτεροῦσιν ἄφρονας

text_en: The man that gives heed to lying visions, is like to him that catches at a shadow, and follows after the wind.
text_la: Quasi qui apprehendit umbram et persequitur ventum, sic et qui attendit ad visa mendacia.
text_el: ὡς δρασσόμενος σκιᾶς καὶ διώκων ἄνεμον οὕτως ὁ ἐπέχων ἐνυπνίοις

text_en: The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another: as when a man's likeness is before the face of a man .
text_la: Hoc secundum hoc visio somniorum, ante faciem hominis similitudo hominis.
text_el: τοῦτο κατὰ τούτου ὅρασις ἐνυπνίων κατέναντι προσώπου ὁμοίωμα προσώπου

text_en: What can be made clean by the unclean ? And what truth can come from that which is false ?
text_la: Ab immundo, quid mundabitur? et a mendace, quid verum dicetur?
text_el: ἀπὸ ἀκαθάρτου τί καθαρισθήσεται καὶ ἀπὸ ψευδοῦς τί ἀληθεύσει

text_en: Deceitful divinations and lying omens and the dreams of evildoers, are vanity:
text_la: Divinatio erroris, et auguria mendacia, et somnia malefacientium, vanitas est :
text_el: μαντεῖαι καὶ οἰωνισμοὶ
